> **Anythinggoes wrote: Thu Feb 29, 2024 5:20 pm**
> Hmm, let's see this lesson put to use. I have this macro:

CastSpellByName("Frostbolt(Rank 1)") - There should be no extra characters or spaces.
If you open the spellbook and the macro window, and then click on the Shift+Right Mouse Button, a line with the spell command will be written to the macro window. For example, /cast Moonfire(Rank 1) - you need to copy Moonfire(Rank 1) to put in quotation marks "", in your macro CastSpellByName("Moonfire(Rank 1)")

I advise you to use notepad++. There's LUA syntax highlighting.

/script local UL,UM,UT,AH=UnitLevel,UnitMana;local function GotSpell(spell,rank) local ix,spellName,spellRank;if not spell then spell="Nature's Swiftness";rank="";end;for ix=1,200 do spellName,spellRank=GetSpellName(ix,"spell") if spellName==nil then return;else if spellName==spell and spellRank==rank then if GetSpellCooldown(ix,"spell")==0 then return true; author: Grizb37
subject: Just some ideas for Feral Class Changes 2.0
content_md:
Druid Baseline Spell Changes.

Barkskin: Now useable in Bear and Cat form.

Savage Bite
Now requires level 40 instead of 54.
Savagely Bite your target causing 100% damage + 85 and causes a high amount of threat.

Swipe (Bear) : Now scales with attack power.

Swipe (Cat) : Hits 3 targets for 75% Normal damage + 45 40 Energy.

Tiger's Fury now persists through shape-shifting.

Frenzied Regeneration: Reduced scaling from 10% Stamina to 5%.

Hurricane: 2sec cast time, no longer channeled. Cool down lowered to 30sec, attack speed debuff lowered to 10%

Rebirth: If used out of combat has a 10 min cool down, if used in combat 30 min

Innervate:
Increases targets mana regeneration by 400%
Increases targets energy regeneration by 100%
Target generates 3 rage per second.

Ever accidently used your innverate on a non mana user? Now it won't be a total waste.

Druid Talent Changes

Thick Hide: All Damage Taken reduced by 2/4/6% while in Bear or Cat Form. (will make it more useful as we have an Armor cap and this becomes useless)

Predatory Strikes: Increases Attack Power by 10% in Cat and Bear Form. (flat % to help us scale better, currently it caps out at +90 flat AP at 60)

Improved Shred: Reduces Energy cost by 9/18 (same value as tbc)

Blood Frenzy: Increases duration of Tiger's Fury by 6/12 sec and increases attack speed by 10/20%.

Leader of the Pack: Increases Critical chance by 4% and haste by 4%
(Idol changed - gives druids options to use other idols rather than forced into using something bis for other players)

Natural Shapeshifter: Reduces Mana cost of forms by 10/20/30% and reduces global cool down on shapeshifting by 0.2/0.3/0.5sec.

Feral Aggresion:
Increases the damage of Ferocious Bite & Savage Bite by 3/6/9/12/15%

Items:

Manual Crowd Pummler.
Charges removed, now increases attack speed by 50% and 10min cool down.

Idol of Moonfang:
Increases critical chance of Moonfire and Starfire by 5%

Idol of Emerald Rot:
Spell power scaling removed (as per recent update)
You deal 85 Nature damage per combo point. (Can Crit)

Idol of Ferocity:
Reduces Energy cost of Claw/Rake/Rip by 3 and increases damage by 10%

Idol of Savagery:
Your Rip and Rake now slow targets movement speed by 30%

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Just some ideas for Feral Class Changes 2.0
content_md:
I think most of these proposals point out legitimate problems feral druids currently face. Some go a little overboard and seem too strong, but it's a good list to highlight current shortcomings of the class.

The only thing not covered at all is the problem with **bears and dodge**. The way TWoW devs design items they clearly think dodge is a great stat for bear tanks (Ring of Nordrassil anyone?), but many high-end tanks disagree. The way the hit table works, dodge generally pushes out regular attacks while leaving crushing blows and critical strikes untouched (meaning it takes out trickle damage but leaves dangerous damage spikes untouched). Dodging many regular attacks can also rage-starve you. I would like to see a talent the remedies these problems. Something that procs on dodges in bear form. It should 1) make sure dodge doesn't have a negative effect and 2) make dodge attractive. I'm thinking of something like:
 **Every time you dodge in bear form, you gain 5 rage and gain a buff giving you 5% attackspeed for 10s that stacks up to 5 times.**

Other than that omission there is only 2 proposals I have issues with:
> **Grizb37 wrote: Wed Feb 21, 2024 10:21 am**
> Frenzied Regeneration: Reduced scaling from 10% Stamina to 5%.
>
>  (Idol changed - gives druids options to use other idols rather than forced into using something bis for other players)
>  Idol of Moonfang:
>  Increases critical chance of Moonfire and Starfire by 5%

Bears are already deeply lacking in **defensive cooldowns** compared to warriors. Frenzied Regen can't remotely measure up to something like Shield Wall. Nerfing it removes one of the few (and quite mediocre) emergency cooldowns we have. I can see the problems in PvP, but in PvE it's pretty fine? It seems very overpowered in dungeons, but is not great at all in raid enviroments. I'm open to toning it down a little (maybe 8%?) but if you go further we should definitely talk about adding new defensive cooldowns that are useful in raids.

And I like Druids not being a completely selfish class like many others that barely interact with others or not at all. Druids are a support class, I'm fine with items that buff our party aura. Also, you mention giving druids options to use other idols - except now there are fewer options. Raid cats use Shred. If you change Moonfang they now have zero idols to use (well, Emerald Rot, but you only need that for the finisher).

Good list, interesting proposals though!

author: Elleshar
subject: Pvp situation for resto druids
content_md:
I would say for the most part druids is overall in a decent spot when it comes to pvp, we win some matchups and we lose others. Rock, paper, scissor the way classic wow has always been. Turtle wow has improved druid somewhat when it comes to feral especially versus it's sad "classic" state which I appreciate, making it viable to play. I haven't tried lots of boomkin but it's alright too from the limited testing I have done.

What I think hasn't gotten any love however is resto druids, specifically alliance resto druids. Why you might ask?

Compared to horde druids we have on alliance side two classes that have instant dispels/purges, making all our HoT spells basically useless. Even if you fake cast rank 1 spells making them go oom is basically non existent, shamans for example here with no gcd totems and near free water shield makes it a moot point to try to outlast or win a mana war against them. When you take in all these factors all resto druids have to rely on is then nature swiftness and healing touch, one of the healing spells with the longest casting time in the game. Good luck not getting silenced when trying to cast it!
Of course you have swiftmend too but you will never get off against a decent priest/shaman. Even warlocks felhunter can easily eat HoTs too.

Now the solution and the way blizzard balanced this in tbc and later expansions was with the introduction of a new spell - Lifebloom. A smaller rejuv basically that heals for a bit if it gets dispelled or finish it's duration. It would solve a lot of problems but if twow doesn't want to implement that I would also suggest some talent that made HoTs have a higher chance to be resisted or not dispelled so easily. This was also introduced in later expansions for druids to deal with this problem.

The reason I bring this up now is because looking at the twow roadmap there might be some future pvp changes in the future, and if they ever bring up rated bgs or rated arenas it would be nice if resto druids were a viable spec to play.

I hope this gives some consideration or discussion for those interested.

author: Tarsis
subject: Re: Improved Mark of the Wild
content_md:
Improved Mark of the Wild, for 5 talents is 100% NOT worth it...
We pick it as Balance/Resto PvE, because the other option is EVEN LESS useful.

Also the calculations Grizb37 made are wrong:

 **- Armor:** who is going to benefit from that + 99 armor? the casters? the melee dps?  NO.
Tanks are those who get hit constantly and so will benefit from an armor boost (even tho 99 extra armor when you already got 10k is almost nothing).
So the CORRECT value should be:
between +200 to +400, depending on how many tanks you have in your specific raid.

 **- Stats:** most classes ONLY benefit from 2 Primary Stats and 1 Secondary out of the 5 stats total.
That ofc varies from class to class, but generally DPS/Tank/Healer classes need 3 stats.
So the CORRECT value should be +12 (stat points) for each Raid member:
 4 (stat points) x 3 (stats affected) x 40 (raid members) = 480 (stats points)

 **- Resistances:** in the majority of raid fights there are no aoe spell damage mechanics and, UNLESS a fight requires everyone to equip Elemental res Gear OR the Raid Boss does multiple spell damage aoe effects during the fight, a +7 is useless.

So to summarize: for 5 talent points spent you get:
 - Armor:    POOP.
 - Stats: +12 per raid member up to 480 total.
 - Resistances:    POOP.

 ***My Assesment? UMGAK.***

author: Grizb37
subject: The new Feral Talents are rubbish.
content_md:
Hello everyone, and thank you for the staff for your continued work on this patch.

I have seen the new talents and taken my time going over them in my head and finding a use for them.

But the thing is, I really wanted to fit these talents into my character. BUT.... I just can't see a use for them at all

 1:
Open wounds:
Increases damage of Claw by 30% if the target is afflicted by Rake, in addition your Rip ability increases your Claw damage by 5% per combo point for 5 seconds.

OK so, the issue with this is that no one uses claw, because even with all these buffs to it and the set up of 5cp rip and rake, this still does less damage than just spamming Shred... I mean I get what the Devs were going for here, but it just falls short massively. Someone on the discord druid channel has been working the maths out on this since release of the new talents, and that's the conclusion he came to.

This talent used to include shred, but was quickly taken off, because it 'nearly did as much damage as a warrior' - now I find this rather silly to be honest.... What exactly is wrong with doing NEARLY as much damage as a warrior? As a cat you have leather armor, alot more squishy NO AOE /cleave , and your heals suck in full feral gear as you have 0 healing and a low mana pool. So this I can't understand.

Anyway moving on to the next talent.

'Feral Adrenaline'
Suffering a physical critical strike while in Bear, Dire Bear or Cat Form, increases your chance to dodge by 45% until you dodge the next physical attack against you. Sounds nice right? Until you read the last part.... 30 second cool down.... I mean what.... 3 talent points for 45% dodge every 30 seconds IF I get Crit?

I'm not sure what the Devs were going for on this as if you dodge you only push hits off the table, not crushes or crits... So honestly I can't recommend anyone take this talent... I think it would need to be 100% chance or change the cool down to 10-15 seconds with 45%.

Last new talent:

Ancient Brutality.

Dodging an attack while in Bear or Dire Bear Form imbues you with the spirit of the ancients. Returning 15% damage dealt as healing and generating 3 rage per second for 5 seconds. Cannot occur more than once every 6 seconds.

Ok this is probably the best of the 3 new talents. But even then I can't see this being used in a raid.... The 15% vampirism won't help much vs a raid boss... Maybe it could have some niche uses in a 5 man with a good geared druid idk... The rage on dodging is the best part about this but as a druid I'm rarely rage starved anyway in bear form...

I honestly think I'd rather just take thick hide than this one

Conclusion:

I think most people are upset because all the other classes got some really nice cool abilities where as feral it feels like we didn't get anything useful .... Just an alternative play style for cat form which requires more effort than power shifting(imo) for less damage? It doesn't make sense to me really.

Not to mention the extra bloat now in the feral tree! There are now 9 more talent points to spend and you can't get them all! Even as a dedicated Bear tank only.

Alot of people like the fact druid in vanilla is a combination of both cat and bear, and you don't have to choose unlike wotlk.... But these new talents took a step in the wrong direction....

Thanks for reading.

author: ForumOLV
subject: In regards to Feral CC2, some ideas.
content_md:
I want to start by saying that I appreciate the team's efforts with all the class changes, including those for Druids. However, I feel that **Feral Druids** are somewhat lacking compared to the improvements other classes have received.

 **Why Do I Say That?**
We’ve been given a new talent called **"Open Wounds"**. While it seems weaker than the current **Powershifting** gameplay on paper, after running some numbers, it could offer a decent alternative for players who don't want to engage with Powershifting. It introduces a new playstyle and makes **Claw** a relevant ability, which I see as a positive direction. I hope that the numbers will reflect it as a viable option.

 **What I Like About the Talent**
What excites me most about this talent is that it makes **Claw** relevant again. That said, there are still a few other abilities that hold very little importance in PvE. Specifically, our **stealth openers**:

- **Pounce**
- **Ravage**

 **Stealth Openers in PvE**
In most PvE situations, Feral Druids have little incentive to use their stealth openers:

- **Pounce** deals negligible damage.
- **Ravage** is outclassed by simply using two **Shreds** in terms of damage output.
 **My Recommendations**

 **Pounce**

Pounce is valuable in PvP for its **stun** component, but the damage portion is extremely low. I noticed that Paladins' **Repentance** will have a PvE component where, if the target is immune to the effect, it still takes damage. I'd like to propose a similar change for **Pounce**:

- If the target is **immune to stuns**, allow the damage from Pounce to stack with every tick (similar to **Curse of Agony**).
- **Damage Scaling Suggestion**: Pounce deals 90 damage every 2 seconds. I suggest a cap of 300% (270 damage every 2 seconds), with the damage increasing by 10% per tick. This would require 60 seconds to reach the cap of 30 stacks (300%).
Since **Pounce** only lasts 18 seconds, I would recommend the following talent tweak to accommodate this:

 **Brutal Impact (2/2)**
- Increases the duration of **Bash** and **Pounce** by 0.5/1 second.
- **Claw** increases the duration of the **Pounce bleed** on the target by 1.5/3 seconds.
With **1 point**, Pounce will drop off over time unless you use finishers and **Clearcasting (CCg)** procs on **Shred**. With **2 points**, you can extend its duration past the global cooldown (GCD), allowing more flexibility to use finishers and CCg procs.

In PvP, this tweak shouldn’t affect balance much, since it only ties to the damage component, which activates when the target is immune. You **could** plan around using it on a stun-immune target, but unless you stay in Cat Form using **Claw** constantly, you wouldn’t gain the full benefit.

 **Ravage**

Let's be honest, Ravage is just a heavy-hitting, frontloaded ability. After I ran the numbers on why Shred was removed from Open Wounds, I found that it was doing as much damage as Ravage, which was interesting to see. Since my Pounce idea is made to accommodate the Open Wounds playstyle of bleed uptime, I would make Ravage the go-to ability for Powershift players.

As such, I have the following idea: Since Powershifting accounts mostly for resetting your energy to spam Shred (and soon, to some extent, Claw, Rake, and Rip), Shred should have an interaction with Ravage. Ravage hits quite hard and would be a bit too much to be able to spam. But what if we rewarded players who Powershift properly with some heavy-hitting hits?

 **REMOVED:** Improved Shred

 **New Talent: Chase the Prey 2/2**
Ravage applies **Chase the Prey** on the target for 20/40 seconds. Using **Shred** on a target afflicted by **Chase the Prey** buffs the druid with stacks of **Ravenous**. Each stack has a 1.5% /3% chance upon **shapeshifting into Cat Form** to allow the usage of **Ravage**. Additionally, this talent reduces the energy cost of Shred by 6 / 12 energy.

 **The idea is the following:**
Reward the druid who starts with Ravage with a chance to use Ravage during the fight. To keep up the debuff, you need to focus on Shredding and Powershifting. Ravage hits very hard, and proper gameplay would allow you to leverage this talent much more often. For PvP, it wouldn't be optimal to use as you would have to maintain Cat Form for a long period of time and Powershift inefficiently for a chance to be able to use Ravage.

With all of these recommendations in mind, I would love to know the thoughts of others on this topic or what else they think Druid needs or would be nice to have in light of the soon upcoming changes. I would appreciate if your thoughts were shared in way that's constructive for the conversation, we have #druid on Turtle's Discord for dooming and memes.

author: Euromind
subject: Re: In regards to Feral CC2, some ideas.
content_md:
In regards to your post I also have some ideas in regard to the CC2 changes to feral druid, both tanking and damage dealing. I’ll give my review and thoughts on the new playstyle in PvE point of view only. I’m by means an expert on feral druids, but not completely new either.

 ****Cat DPS****
Right now, the way for feral DPS seem to be power shifting and the rotation goes roughly like
- Shred till 4-5 combo points and then Ferocious Bite, while power shifting to refill your energy.

- Occasionally throw in a Tiger’s Fury for the 12% haste if you got the chance.
With the new class changes you get the option to use “bleed build”. However, if you want to continue as before. The only thing we get is like 18% more haste in your rotation and the combo points follows if you switch target That’s it.

“Cat Form’s Combo Points will no longer vanish upon switching targets, but instead reset when applying combo points on a new target.”

If you want to try the new “bleed build” you got a few more things to look out for in comparison to powershifting.
- You need to keep track of 3 uptimes
o        Tiger’s Fury - 12 sec.
o	Rip - 12 sec.
o	Rake - 9 sec.
I did some testing self-buffed (no consumes) with 28% crit chance and not power shifting, and it was not easy to keep all 3 abilities active at the same time, and I surely did not manage to weave in Ferocious Bite.

One of the perks though is that we don’t have to think about hitting the back.

Don’t get me wrong, I absolutely love an active playstyle, but I also like to perform well in raid and pull my own weight. I think one of the reasons some classes perform better than others are because of its simplicity.

When I play my “boring” mage I just tab from target to target and cast frost bolt. There’s not much to look out for beside mana and aggro.

My suggestion to bleed build is to automate at least some of the abilities. Either by:
- Crits or ability crits refresh the rake bleed.

- Finishers refresh Tiger’s Fury.

- Or something else…
Warrior’s impale talent automatically apply bleed, their Flurry talent gives them the 30% haste (for 3 swings)

 ****Feral Tanking****
Right now, most of our threat comes from MCP and thanks for removing that item. But then we are down to 30% haste from enrage for a shorter duration.

In comparison to feral DPS, tanking is a very passive playstyle that mostly reply on your gear rather than your skills (of cause it matter a lot to know the boss mechanics, but I’m talking about our buttons to press)

We got Maul, Swipe and Savage Bite

- Maul consumes our rage and auto attack for more threat, but also uses our white swing that provides us with rage.

- Swipe got buffed a bit but is used to keep aggro on more target.

- Savage Bite is also buffed with more threat and can be clever used with clearcasting proc as it cost a bit more (25 rage).
So besides managing our rage we don’t got much going on for us. We don’t have an active/reactive ability to avoid attacks. My suggestion would be to add something to that playstyle, so it doesn’t only come down to how good your gear is.

With the new class changes we are going even further away from an active playstyle with Frenzied Regeneration increased from 3 to 6 min. and Barkskin from 1 to 10 min.

I think it’s interesting that dodge has become somewhat useful, but if as some people mention that druids can become crit immune, then talents like Feral Adrenaline become redundant.

Obviously I haven’t tested Ancient Brutality so it’s hard to comment on, but I think it’s nice to get something from dodge.

What could change towards a more active and skill-based tank play? I don’t know, but you could leave Barkskin as it is and let it be used in forms? You trade some threat for survivability. Nice for enrage phases or if you get low on HP and healers are dead and IF you have enough threat to sacrifice.

 **Items**
I don’t know how the new tier set are going to affect us, but out playstyle shouldn’t be tailored to a specific item, we saw that with MCP and Wolfsheart helm.

And while we are at it. I think it would be a good idea to move the Wolfsheart enchant to idol slot or just make it baseline part of the Furor talent. So we don’t miss out on a head enchant.

 **Talents**
A last thing about the changes. It seems like we need 3 specs in feral now which I think it’s a shame. The devs should try to combine some of the talents so we don’t need 3 different feral specs.

- Feral tanking (and we don’t even have talent points enough for a full tanking spec)

- Raid Power Shifting spec (as it still seems to be our best option)

- Single target farm spec (I find myself using claw a lot when farming mobs in the open world. I think this could boost our farm potential)

author: Romy
subject: A few thoughs on the new feral DPS
content_md:
So no more MCP. So TWOW has given us some new damage boosts.

Will the new boosts actually help with our DPS in raids? I'm not sure it will. Here are my thoughts.

Previously, feral did not use claw, rake, or rip during most raid encounters. The rotation most ferals use is shred to 5 combo points then ferocious bite. Neither shred nor ferocious bite were buffed at all, so the question is, will claw, rake and rip now be used in a dps rotation during raids. If the answer is yes, Rake/Claw/Rip rotation is better than Shred/Bite, that is great news. I don't think this will be the case though.

So what's the problem? Feral will be ridiculously overtuned in pvp if Rake/Claw/Rip are that powerful. This is similar to a time in vanilla, I believe it was the very beginning of Lich King that ferals were bleed gods for about 2 months before blizzard nerfed them to the ground again. You could literally pounce, mangle, rake, claw, rip and then walk away and watch any non-healer die from the bleed damage.

I am not sure so early in the patch if Rake/Claw/Rip will out damage Shred/Bite, but if it doesn't then feral just got the nerf stick, and if it does, I can't wait to bleed the heck out of everyone in PVP.

Anyone with after patch raid experience, please let me know if Rake/Claw/Rip is out dpsing Shred/Bite.

The vampirism talent is definitely good, and especially good for fights with multiple targets since you dodge more, but other than that you're not spending any more points than you used to (I put two points into the vamp talent since I had everything I needed with 2 to spare), and should be able to afford everything you need as a feral, furor and omen included. Most of these new talents, unfortunately just... Kinda suck. Don't take 'em.

I'm going to concur with this.

Personally I didn't take Open Wounds or Feral Adrenaline. I did put 2 points into Blood Frenzy since I think that's just too good to pass up in both cat and bear forms and then I spent my final two points in Ancient Brutality which...honestly, for 2 points still gets you quite a bit of value. Having said all of that I didn't take the Berserk talent since I'm only running dungeons and not doing raid content. Depending on what content you're doing there is flexibility with this for sure. author: Glowingfrom
subject: Buff/Debuff limit makes feral dps change meaningless
content_md:
From the new feral dps talent change, you can clearly see the devs is trying really hard to push powershifting out of feral dps rotation. With increased lasting time and damage of Tiger's fury/Blood Frenzy and losing TF when shifting out, claw + rake + rip combo can easily outperform  shred + powershift, even with Improved Shred. But, this happens only when :

 1) Rake and Rip can actually land on the target
 2) You have the 2 buff slots for TF and BF

However, in a 40man raid like 10+ Warriors dotting deep wounds, and numerous pally buffs, temporary healing buffs,  the above situation just does not exist. So, basically druid still need to shred/powershifting, but this time, without MCP.

To be honest, I really cannot understand the logic of pushing druid to use bleeding rotation without increasing/removing buff/debuff limits. So, Why change? Why not just delete feral dps from the game?

Druids are so bad compared to other healers and bring zero utility other than a battle res compared to other classes. Healing is not and has never been about raw output for performance.

Depends on what you find fun to play.  I'm fairly new to Turtle WoW with no level 60's yet, but here is my groove as a casual player that plays for fun/versatility more than anything else.

Prior to the big change patch this last month I recently leveled my NE Druid up to 51 via Balance spec (after purchasing the donation store Glyph to change Moonkin form into Astral form instead, since I detest Moonkin form).

After the patch, I decided to continue solo/questing as a "Moonglow" (non-Moonkin use) hybrid Balance/Resto spec instead, since the new talent layout makes it more viable & appealing, & going in & out of Moonkin form to heal/top-off while solo is super annoying & clunky. author: Fornow
subject: Re: Balance druid aoe/questing spec after the patch ?
content_md:
I don't see balance druid being good at AOE like mage or paladin. You simply lack the right spells for it. Currently leveling a druid and switching back and forth between balance and feral. Overall feral still seems a bit stronger at my level (40+) but balance is still viable.

The best balance spec for leveling is pretty much going to fill out the entire balance tree minus:
- gale winds (hurricane slows attack speed)

- improved nature's grasp (just the 1 in initial point is enough)

- only 2/3 into natural shape shifter
This leave you with 5 points which could well go into Furor from Resto tree. The instant rage upon entering bear from is very useful for emergency stuns/charges.

Going deeper into restoration tree seems like a trap, you'd be investing way too many points before you get to the good stuff (genesis for increased damage over time). Sylvan blessing is amazing, when chain killing enemies it has near 100% up time. Don't know why you want to skip that. So you don't really benefit much from meditation (15% mana regen in combat) either.

This is how I would allocate points for the first 40 levels:
![Image](https://i.imgur.com/KaW3sjb.png)

My rotation is usually:
- (for tough enemies:) open with wrath from max range and before the projectile hits another wrath or starfire

- insect swarm, move backward during global cool down

- moonfire, move backwards during global cool down

- Starfire while enemy runs toward you

- for tough foes or quick hitting enemies like cats: entangling roots to prevent spell push back, move back a little

- another star fire

- finish off the enemy with wrath and punching; remember owl punches can also trigger omen of clarity
For mana efficiency the enemy ideally dies when your dots run out. Remember to synchronize your spells with the enemy attack speed for less chance of spell push back.

I almost never have to drink, instead I go into cat form a bit when I'm low on mana. It helps if you have an add-on for quickly equipping a feral gear set while your in it. Thanks to omen of clarity you get a lot of free abilities in (best used on rip as it costs the most energy). I also level up 1st aid anyways, using bandages conserves mana and let's me stay in form.

author: Kangaraxxus
subject: Moonkin DPS Calculator updated to 1.17.2
content_md:
[Calculator itself is a Google Spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1IACK4CltzOMmULWtprWE9lV86zl2La3fUZufOw6we9g/edit?usp=sharing)
You need to do File->Make a Copy to be able to feed it with your inputs

Right now it works for one specific rotation, assuming you keep it ideally, and does not account for ramp up period or rotation breaking up due to bad luck or extra luck with crits. This is what you should get on average during long static fights like Patchwerk.
Six pieces of T3 considered to give static 1% dps increase, but in reality it is more complex and i don't have enough time/courage to improve it. How did i get 1% though - assuming we keep both dots on a target, chances that debuff was up during last 6 seconds (3 ticks from IS + 2 ticks from MF = 5) is 1 - (1-0.08)^5 = 0.34 On avarage
 34% chance to have 3% dmg boost is 1% dmg boost.

But main value of this calculator is to get some estimation on a stats value, which i think it is doing just fine.

Final note about HASTE.
![Image](https://i.ibb.co/6wfd0C4/TWOW-GCD.png)
And yes, Haste is fine on a boomie, so is T3 set

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Please Make Feral Adrenaline Useful
content_md:
> Suffering a physical critical strike while in Bear, Dire Bear or Cat Form increases your chance to dodge by 15/30/45% until you dodge the next physical attack against you. This effect can only occur once every 30 seconds

I think that this talent is useful for tanking and PvP.
Bears can't get crit immunity, so the talent smoothes out peaks of critical damage.
For cats in pvp is is very good against any melee, except warrior. But even in that case, you get additional critical Overpower no often than once in 30 secs.

It can be tweaked to reduce timer between occurences to help in PvE.
Other way around - it doesn't have to give dodge. Instead it can reduce damage of melee critical strikes by 100%. This way, druids won't be devastated by warriors.
Though, why should druid vs warrior fight be different? I imagine warrior as hard-counter against druids.

author: Eyeburn
subject: Re: Tiger's Fury stay active on Powershifting
content_md:
Powershifting has its own charm, but it ultimately holds back feral dps by making it extremely reductive, just spam shred.  It's not a good basis for rebalancing feral dps on this server because it is based on an oversight.  Turning wolfshead into an enchant is an easy solution, but a long term solution should seek to eliminate the playstyle as the only viable one.  What this server has is effectively TBC's cat rotation, and it's very dry.

Wrath cat was terrible, but there is a way to give cat a rotation that isn't endless bleed and buff management.  Powershifting disregards any intended rotation to spam Shred.  If Tiger's Fury and Rake are worth the energy and combo point costs, you can build a real rotation for cat.  Letting feral benefit from 'on hit' effects would also be easier to balance.  Vanilla cat damage can very easily sky rocket with small buffs due in large part to powershifting exaggerating their effects.

author: Jammyzz
subject: Feedback for Druid Balance Changes 20th December
content_md:
DRUID

Now several weeks into our second round of class changes, we we’re able to observe how our druid changes played out in the hands of our community. We are overall happy with how Balance and Restoration play out, even if the former still has some minor things that can be ironed out regarding the reward or proper rotation. Feral Combat on the other hand is a double-edged sword at the moment. While both Bear and Cat are performing well, Bear even more than we imagined, there are still details left we wish to address. In case of Feral Cat, we wish to explore and expand their identity more beyond the 20-year-old Powershifting and add power to non-Powershifters.

Its great that you're introducing a new playstyle that doesn't involve powershifting, for the minority that don't like it, however nothing has been added to the tried and trusted / loved Powershifting Cat,  Most players had to beg and doom on the discord initially just to get a slight upgrade to Improved Shred.

Open Wounds: Effect reworked to the following: "Increases the damage of Claw by 10/20/30% and Ferocious Bite by 3/4/5% for each of your active Bleed effects on the target."

Can you expand this abit please, it seems a bit vague, so does this mean that 1 Combo point of Rip on the target will now grant +30% Claw damage?, Consider adding abit of Shred damage here for the powershifting cats, maybe +4% per bleed.

Feral Aggression and Open Wounds now increase Ferocious Bite's total damage instead of its base damage.

Its okay, I Guess, from my testing in bis gear, this is around +2% extra Ferocious Bite Damage, heck its better than nothing.

Developer Comment: We’ve taken steps in establishing a new identity for Feral Cats before, enhancing their abilities through application of their Bleed effects. We’d like to go further with this design by enabling Open Wounds to all three Bleed effects available to Feral Cats and including Ferocious Bite into its functionality.

New Identity? But the majority of people who roll a Feral Druid in Vanilla, prefer the powershifting build, please dont stray too far away from this, yes there is a vocal minority that hate powershifting , so this is basically saying, You can powershift if you want, but this will not be support in the future... The current Tier sets seem to favor your new bleed build.

Ancient Brutality: Periodic ticks of your Bleed effects restore 2/3/4 Energy while in Cat Form. Dodging an attack while in Bear or Dire Bear Form regenerates 1/2/3 rage per second for 5 seconds. This effect can only occur once every 9 seconds.
Developer Comment: Taking this further, we also allow ticks of their Bleed effects to restore energy. This is one of many steps taken to deepen the synergies brought forth by Bleeds. However, the Bear side of this talent was outperforming for the bonus it gives and the amount of uptime. To combat this, we’ve increased the cooldown on the talent and removed the extra vampirism to even out its power.

I think this has been said before, that just making talents for Bear only or Cat only, is not what people want, so thanks for adding Cat to this talent aswel. That said I think this one has fallen short of the mark, the Ancient Brutality, was not overpowered in its previous form at all, and now removing the Vampirism part of it completely kills the talent for Bears, as that was the best part, regards to the energy return, It seems a little low to make an impact, perhaps 2/4/6 would be better?

Feral Adrenaline: Dodge bonus increased from 15/30/45% to 20/40/60%.
Developer Comment: We are increasing the Dodge chance to make this talent more reliable when it is triggered.

Unfortuantly this changes nothing, the dodge chance was not the issue, the long 30 second ICD, is the biggest issue with this talent, making it feel like it hardly triggers , consider reducing the cooldown to 10-15 seconds maximum, or better yet change it from dodge to damage reduction on the next phsyical attack.

Swipe: Attack Power scaling reduced from 6% to 4%.

This was 8% orignally, this just feels unwarranted, swipe was critting 280 ish in BIS gear with full raid buffs, hardly overpowered, maybe the threat should have been dialed back, as some cat DPS enjoyers loved going bear for AOE cleave with this scaling, now this wont be feasible, especially with the Savage Bite nerf below.

Frenzied Regeneration: Cooldown reduced from 6 to 5 minutes.

Developer Comment: Frenzied Regeneration feels a bit too weak right now, so we’re giving it power back by reducing its cooldown.

Unfortuantly this adds no power back to it, no one will really feel a 1 minute cooldown decrease, this spell has always been a 3 minute cooldown during is lifetime from various expansions, the healing you have nerfed it to, is now barely stronger than its vanilla version, which makes the cooldown increase unwarranted.
Suggestions: reduce cooldown back to baseline 3minutes or add 10% healing instead of current 8%.

Savage Bite: Cooldown increased from 6 to 9 seconds.

Developer Comment: While we see Feral Bears as a threat focused tank, their overall power overshot its target. We’re dialing their threat a bit back with this change.

Terrible change, Bear is stuck at a 2.5 sec swing timer, and this is their only Snap Threat ability, if just one of these misses, waiting 9 seconds for another will feel godawful.
I would not reduce the damage of this ability either, as it does less damage than a Maul, and is bears only real Instant damage deal ability for single target, which will heavily nerf their damage, which wasnt brilliant to start with.

Grizzled Hide (Feral Tier 3 8 Set): Duration increased to 15 seconds, maximum stacks down from 10 to 4, Damage reduction increased from 1% to 2%.
Developer Comment: Following Savage Bite’s increased cooldown, we’re giving Grizzled Hide a little bit more wiggle room to play with.

No one really likes this set bonus, it should just be removed and replaced for something else, Put the effect at 6% damage reduction on Thick Hide talent, which is a useless talent after Bears hit Armor cap.

author: Eyeburn
subject: Re: Why Tier Sets for Feral dps provide so much intelligen
content_md:
> **Drubarrymooer wrote: Mon Feb 17, 2025 4:25 pm**
> Powershifting is amazing and I hope it stays forever.  There are a lot of people who enjoy it.

No, it isn't amazing.  It was a fun discovery that let feral dps be relevant next to the horde of warriors in vanilla.  Here's what actually happened:

 - Bear tank underrated, but multiple tanks are necessary in vanilla
 - Dual spec doesn't exist and multiple prot warriors aren't good when not needed for this or that fight
 - Bear is a actually a hybrid spec, and a hybrid cat does more damage when not tanking than a prot warrior
 - Cat dps still isn't great, but then we found MCP and wolfshead powershifting

Now our offtanks are bears that can do respectable damage when not tanking.  This was fun and cool, and it caused the clearly spec breaking exploit that is powershifting to be overlooked.  Not least of all, it was overlooked because cat dps wasn't exactly top tier even with powershifting and MCP.  Fast forward many years later to pservers, and now warriors are fury/prot, which ultimately just meant that bears and warriors were equally strong as off tanks without sacrificing much raid dps from boss to boss.

Powershifting doesn't have any depth.  It's exploiting an overlooked combination of wolfshead and furor to create energy from mana.  The problem is that it's a broken effect.  Pressing Shred is always a top priority.  Any complexity in powershifting is just spending your sub 60 energy value, if possible, before shifting again to press Shred.  And this interaction is broken.  It was broken enough to prop wolfshead helmet as bis all the way through TBC.  Let that sink in, a level 42 rare helmet remained bis over the strongest level 70 headgear in the game in TBC.

Holding onto powershifting ruins anything that could be done with feral dps.  There is no way to buff anything that feral dps can do in a way that doesn't just make powershifting stronger.  That's why it's currently breaking feral dps, and try to realize that "breaking" doesn't mean that feral dps is massively ahead of everything else.  A "broken" mechanic is one that is unhealthy for the class.  In the case of feral druid, spending every GCD to hit shred breaks the spec.

author: Greenaniline
subject: Feral tank stat priority
content_md:
Hello, does anyone know which is the "agreed" general stat priority for bears?

I see a lot of players, mostly fresh 60s going by what i assume is the Icyveins stat priority that being Armor>Stamina>Defense>Agility/Dodge>Hit.

The other bears i see, generally with bis gear, go full agi, str and stamina. Completley disregarding defense. I understand that it may depend on the boss fight, but generally, is it better to aim for offensive stats rather than defensive?

author: Drubarrymooer
subject: Re: Feral tank stat priority
content_md:
You actually want a fair amount of dodge because of ancient brutality.  Outside of naxx, you generally don't worry about defense.  Even then, you're probably not going to hit cap unless you go out of your way to do so.  I would say go armor till cap/stam/hit/agi+str.  Now that the tier gear has multiple sets, it's a lot easier to gear.

I'm not the best druid out there though.  Some might have better advice or different thoughts on stat prio.

Depends on the fight, most of the bosses can be done with a cat set and tank jewerly, so

hit until cap, agi and stam

become the priority. Then there's bosses in raids who hit you hard or you're not sure if they hit hard. On those cases you go

hit until cap, defense, stamina, armor.

Some bosses in bwl can hit you very hard if you aren't careful, so does twins in aq40 and bosses with limited healing like Erennius, maexxna or loatheb

author: Fugus
subject: Question: Feral Hybrid gamplay.
content_md:
I have been away for awhile waiting for the devs to finish what they are doing to decide what I want to do (No point in being a Tauren if the Night Elves outclass them in every way as a druid).

But it appears they are trying to destroy the hybrid gameplay of Feral and trying to force us to specialize like they did in WotLK which destroyed much of the fun for me.

Are they REALLY trying to destroy one of the core draws of being a feral druid like that or are they still trying to address it later? Because I just took a look at the talent trees and it is bloated to the point you can't really play as a proper hybrid like you could originally.

Can understand getting rid of our reliance on the manual crowd pummeler, I could even agree with them getting rid of our reliance on powershifting if they wanted. But being able to go from Cat to Bear without having to respec was one of the most fun parts of it for me.

In the old TBC days I loved going into raids alternating between cat and bear as the encounter dictated, I loved going in as a DPS only to drop out in throw off heals when things got rough or go bear and hold the boss if the main tank went down to finish it. I actually had setup a pure DPS set, a pure Tank set, and a hybrid set where I could be decent as both. I might not have topped the charts when I wore the hybrid set but I definitely pulled my weight and saved countless wipes and when I went full cat, I could compete and even top the DPS charts (until endgame where our scaling hit a wall) and in pure tank was actually enjoyed by the healers (except in pugs where the DPS couldn't help but AoE out the gate even knowing the bears were crap for AoE threat).

That's sad. I joined here to play something closer to what I enjoyed which was TBC style Feral druid. I hated when they tried to break them up in WotLK, it killed much of the joy of the game to me and I could never get into alts either. I liked being the switch hitter that could switch roles in a fight if need be, even if I wasn't the greatest at it at that time.

If I wanted to be a rogue, I would have rolled one, if I wanted to be a warrior I would have rolled one. I didn't roll feral to be half a feral and ignore the other half.

I thought the point of much of this was to improve on the old stuff and fix the classes without changing their identities, removing the hybrid nature of Feral is removing one of the core parts of it's identity for those who actually enjoyed it.

You can make a cat DPS viable and a bear tank viable without actually breaking them up with their specs. Their gear accounts for a lot of that. I would rather lose power shifting than lose my hybrid nature.

If they are going to address issues that actually needs to be addressed for feral druids, then let them use their cats speed, PvP set bonus, and entangling roots indoors.

author: Noobikscube
subject: Boomkin Tier and Haste
content_md:
In CC2 Boomkin received some changes that breathed a lot of life into the CC1 1 button spec. These changes have been well received by the players and have made the class more interesting, more fun, and have a higher skill ceiling. The most impactful talent added being Eclipse.

Boomkin flavor has always been about crit. They provide a large crit aura to fellow casters, they have strong crit modifiers, whenever they crit they get .5 seconds off their next cast and then in CC2 Boomkin got Eclipses proccing upon Wrath and Starfire crits. Making crit an even more valuable and necessary stat. Literally living and dying by the crit.

When we look at this new play style that lives and breathes if they are critting or not, one would hope that these new alt tier sets would help support this new iteration of boomkin.

When looking at tier 3 and 3.5 balance sets they do not appear to be on the same page as the class direction itself. We have haste stacked on multiple items. Is haste useless? No, but apart from spell power the Boomkin stat prio is Crit>Hit>Haste.

Haste was also added to other alt tier sets, like arcane mage, and affliction lock, but their new kits actually scale with haste and is a sought after stat. Please consider removing the haste and making room in the stat budget for more crit.

author: kierova
subject: Re: Boomkin Tier and Haste
content_md:
One of the things that has been communicated to me in the past via the devs (and by example with the new and recent changes to our boon system in Balance of All Things), is that the developers seem to think that haste will compensate for our ultimate and utter lack of crit.

While haste will indeed, mathmatically speaking, allow us to caste a greater number of abilities, there is no failsafe nor bad luck protection when it comes to the all-too-reliant crit that we need in order to do comparable damage to other casters. For example, just last week on Grobbulus, my first Wrath crit occured at approximately 50% of the boss's HP. I did not receive another meaningful crit until the boss was at 4% HP, while Arcane Eclipse was well off cooldown, and then the boss was dead. I was able to use one 15 second window of my Eclipse buff on a fight that lasted over a minute. This feels absolutely awful, and no amount of haste will prevent this from continuing to happen time and time again.

Yes, haste is not a meaningless stat, but it is by far the least valuable stat for the current Balance kit, and it is both disappointing and concerning that the developers continue to not only ignore, but argue against and laugh about the current state of both our current tier gearing options, but future tier sets as well.

Give us the crit and hit we are constantly starved of. Give us a form of bad luck protection with a cooldown that can force proc an eclipse (why do shamans have Elementual Mastery, but we don't have something similar?). And stop pretending that the "hybrid tax" is real, and treat Balance like the proper caster our new cc2 kit wants us to be.

author: Eyeburn
subject: Re: Seperating the pounce stun/bleed effect
content_md:
Powershifting needs to be removed from feral dps if the tree is going to get anywhere from where it is now.  You can't make shred the best possible button to press every GCD, keep powershifting, and expect any other changes to affect player choices.

Make rake free and lasts 30s?  We're still powershifting.
Remove the energy cost from rip?  We're still powershifting.
Make claw refresh all bleeds on the target?  We're still powershifting.
Add a 3rd rotational bleed?  We're still powershifting.
Add a chance for bleed ticks to refresh tiger's fury?  We're still powershifting.

These are all exaggerated and extreme examples, yet none of it would push out powershifting; all of them would improve powershifting further.  Powershifting stopped being interesting after it's initial discovery.  There's no depth to it, and even less complexity, which is why it thrives.  It's easy to play and performs better than any other variant way to play feral dps.  You'll find that same combination in any "S rank" playstyle across all games.  Performance + ease of use = S tier and broken strategies.  Powershifting is broken.

I appreciate that turtle WoW exists at all and is run by people who care to improve upon vanilla without butchering vanilla, but they've missed the mark substantially with feral dps.

author: Synlapse
subject: Resto druid could be more fun
content_md:
Great server and great class changes for the most part! I have more fun playing feral and moonkin than in classic. The same cannot be said for resto druids, unfortunately. This is not a post about power, only about how it feels to play. While HoT healing is definitely the way to go for druids, the tree of life form brings it all down imho.

In order of importance:

 **Slow**
One reason I went with druid is because its mobility. however the tree is slow. It feels like having a constant hamstring on and its just not fun. Wasting mana to shift out just to not fall behind your dungeon group is not fun gameplay. In pvp it's a death sentence.

 **Visual**
Some people might like looking like a tree, but i appreciated that the healing druid was the one druid spec where you could see your gear and your char. It would be much better to make the tree visual an optional glyph for those who like it.

 **No offensive spells**
It might not matter in raids, but in dungeons its no fun to be cut off from all damage abilities. We can't even wand. All we can do is stand there or try to melee, which is of course a terrible idea. Especially strange since the talent Genesis, required for tree form, improves dots.

 **Limited spells**
Tree of life cuts off healing touch when there already are so few healing spells. I don't mind making hots the main/best way to heal, but how does this artificial limit make the class more fun? Also tranquility is now on such a long cooldown it feels like it does not exist, further limiting the healing arsenal.

My proposal - change tree of life talent to:

Lifegiving Grace
While this aura is active the healing power of nearby party members is increased by an amount equal to 20% of your spirit and the mana cost of heal over time spells is reduced by 20%, however the mana cost of healing touch is increased by 20%.
OPTIONAL Glyph: tree of life

author: Sylveria
subject: Re: Resto druid could be more fun
content_md:
From my understanding (at least when it came to raiding) druids were never meant to be the big healers. On Blizzard Servers with TBC and the ability Lifebloom, the Druid established itself as a sort of "Support-Healer" who was filling the gaps between the big heals from priests and paladins/shamans. I raided as tree-druid during TBC and I enjoyed my spot.
Unfortunately: Yes the Resto isn't really fun here on Turtle.. at least not yet. I'm still a strong advocate of adding Lifebloom here, which, at least in my opinion, is a Must Have for the Tree of Life, since its only 2 spells are rejuvenation and regrowth (and Swiftmending), since Healing Touch isn't an option for this form.
Though I'm more of a Vanilla player, TBC was imo the definitive version for resto druids.
(afair Lifebloom got heavily nerfed with WotLK, rendering the resto druid kinda useless again).

I'm not pro player and don't calculate everything through, i merely give my opinion on how the class "felt" from playing.

Regarding the visuals: Someone suggested here on the forum to add a glyph to shop similar to the "Glyph of Stars" for the Moonkin form, but instead a "Glyph of Emerald Dream" with a green shimmer for the Tree form. I'd like to see that. We would have a visible caster form (while technically still in tree form) and Turtle could earn a bit more for the server. Win-Win.

author: Spriggit
subject: Re: Resto druid could be more fun
content_md:
I have to agree with Elleshar. I have healer characters of every other class and druid is by far the least interesting to play when done as a straight up healing spec'd tree.

I have a few unrelated ideas that would make the healing side more interesting. One idea would be that tree form would permit a few other spells to be cast - maybe even just wrath. Something low mana and spammable for Omen of Clarity clicks.

Another idea would be to have balance/restoration capstones to include a mana-free shapeshift every 30 seconds or so. This would be let you, say, start by doing a little physical dps in cat form until the party suffers some hits, pop into tree form to lay some HoTs in, then pop back to cat to keep dpsing (would be kinda low dps in healing gear, but it'd be 'free*'.

One more interesting option would be to have all forms available to every druid once they've reached level 40. The forms would more or less be as they are now - maybe the benefits could be toned down until speccing into the appropriate skill tree. The capstones for balance/resto would allow for all druid spells to work in moonkin/tree form.

This might seem a bit unbalanced as, say, a Moonkin that can cast healing touch; but hey, paladins and shamans are already super high AC healers and aren't necessarily considered unbalanced. This would put druid healers (in pvp) on a par with those classes to some extent.

subject: Re: Vampirism for Bears?
content_md:
As a tank in raids you should never prioritize vampirism. You need to be as beefy as you can. Its others job to keep that healthbar full.

As a tank you typically will deal somewhere in the 500-800 dps range. While often taking  800 or more DPS yourself.
 50-80 healing per second is a drop in the bucket and you should only get it if you are tanky enough and have no threat problems already, or if you have literally no alternative gear.

One of the things I loved about druid was the different quests to get their different forms.
I like that part of old MMORPGs, the part where you have to take a break from leveling and questing and grouping and just go do an important quest line by yourself.

If they implemented such a reskin, I'd also be in favor of a quest for that as well.

________
And finally, there are a lot of potential animal form skin variants that should be in the donation shop.
This is a huge miss for the team.

author: Slade1994
subject: Cat DPS suggestion
content_md:
Hi EU Turtle WoW community,

I’m a Feral Druid main from the SEA server. I’ve been playing Cat DPS since Nostalrius, through Classic 2018, and now on Turtle WoW. I really appreciate all the changes made to improve Cat DPS, but I still have some suggestions to further refine Feral Druid gameplay.

Rake: Direct damage remains unchanged. Bleed duration increased to 18 seconds, and bleed damage is relatively increased.

Rip: Bleed duration increased to 18 seconds, and the bleed damage per combo point is increased.
New effect: Ferocious Bite refreshes the duration of Rip on the current target.

Ferocious Bite:
•	Remove the energy-to-damage conversion effect, OR significantly improve the energy conversion ratio, as the current effect is too weak.
•	New effect: If the target is affected by Rip, Ferocious Bite will refresh Rip’s duration.

Tiger’s Fury:
•	Damage bonus increased by 50 points. The buff should persist in Humanoid Form until it expires or until the player shifts into an animal form other than Cat Form (e.g., it should not carry over to Bear Form).
•	Reasoning: The 20% attack speed bonus from talents persists outside Cat Form, so why shouldn’t the damage bonus? Additionally, since Feral Druids still rely on powershifting, the damage buff should remain.

Pounce:
•	This skill has seen little use in recent patches. Due to the “Open Wounds” effect, it’s sometimes used in solo elite as well, but the overall effectiveness remains poor. Suggested changes:
•	Increase bleed damage.
•	Base stun duration increased from 2 seconds to 3 seconds.
•	Remove the positional requirement (no longer requires attacking from behind).

Claw:
•	Currently capped at Rank 5, while Shred is already at Rank 6.
•	Given the current feral design, we improving Claw’s damage through bleed effects, should there be a Rank 6 Claw to increase its base damage accordingly?

⸻

Dash:
•	Currently, the buff disappears immediately when shifting out of Cat Form.
•	Suggested change: The buff should persist and continue to provide its effect when shifting back into Cat Form.

Auto-attacks:
•	Feral Druids are the only Melee DPS class unable to counter the glancing blow mechanic.
•	According to current talents and test results from raids, auto-attacks now contribute the highest DPS for Feral Druids in PvE, surpassing Shred.
•	Suggested change: Allow Leader of the Pack or weapons with Feral Attack Power to grant Druids their own weapon skill, resolving the issue of glancing blows. (Even Beast Mastery Hunter pets have weapon skills!) ![😭](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f62d.svg)

Ancient Brutality
•	No changes for Bear Form.
•	Energy regeneration from Cat Form bleeds is currently too low.
•	Suggested change: Increase energy regeneration to 4/6/8 to help Feral Druids reduce reliance on powershifting.

I understand that class balance is important—I’m just sharing my thoughts, and hopefully, some of these suggestions can help. Thanks for providing this platform! I love Turtle WoW!

When facing three or more mobs, I’ve found that the most effective way to deal damage is actually switching to Bear Form, which feels really frustrating as a Cat player.

subject: Re: Cat DPS suggestion
content_md:
Seems you've double-posted.

A little off-topic, but see how it relates to the issue with Bleeds: Warrior has a DpS Tier Set Bonus which causes inflicted Critical Strikes a chance to refresh an already-applied Rend on the victim. Rend by itself is weak, its scaling was further changed in a way that doesn't make sense, and the Talent was nerfed and that has made it even more undesirable (it's just a prerequisite to get to Deep Wounds and especially Impale), and generally, Rend is left unused when it comes to endgame play. It's more of a situational PvP Ability now, against Stealth Classes and kiting. This change, however, adds some value back to it: you use Rend only once, and then leave it to your Crits to refresh it, potentially for the entire rest of the fight.

Feral could make good use of this in some form for their own Bleeds.

author: Noephix
subject: Re: Is powershifting still meta? Best Rotation for max DPS
content_md:
Many clueless answers here.

No, powershifting is not meta anymore, on everything else you skip shifting and achieve the same (even slightly better) results. Meta is non-shifting bleeds+claw spam. You use the old rotation only on bleed-immune targets (those are plentiful in molten core and then go extinct until kara40).

Item devs seem completely oblivious to what feral actually needs and most of new items are garbage, so we still use the same old AQ40 gear while other specs get full-slot upgrades in Naxx and Kara40.

My best cat tip is to go boomkin instead if you plan to raid high-end content.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Panzerkin
content_md:
I can be convinced but for now I'm against this because of gameplay reasons.
My PoV is this:
You have the druid, a class which can play all 4 roles. Asking that the form designed to be a caster could also tank or melee is mixing up the roles and feels too much.
I like diversity in playstyles but giving an example about how this one feels:
I'm a shaman main. This feels like not only asking that shamans could tank on this server, it's specifically asking that even though we have a shaman tank, I wanna tank with my elemental shaman.
I feel this is specially weird because even if you are fully specced as a moonkin, you could probably tank better in bear form than in moonkin form even after these changes.

But if it breaks nothing (including PVP), I can be convinced. Diversity in playstyles is the thing I like.

content_md:
> **Melancalos wrote: Thu Apr 10, 2025 7:30 am**
> you saying the weapon hits almost like a caster wand with no AP or melee hit?

Yes, if you dont gear for it, but compared to casterwands it not only scales with physical stats if you choose to wear them, but you also have access to purpose build leather dps gear on druid.
Now you can gear for spelldamage over physical, but then you are just not playing your meme spec to its fullest potential.

Assuming you play to not intereupt your auto attacks, you get ~1 cast of insect swarm and 3 casts of moonfire (only one of which maxrank so your dot can tick trough) within a 12 second window. You get 14.4% of your spelldamage per second in dmg.
Thats pityful amounts of scaling. Most casters boast 30-40% of their spelldamage a second.
Some napkin maths equates the value of one point of spellpower to be less than 2 AP. 2 AP is a hell of a lot easier to get than 1 spellpower.

There is nothing wrong in playing a meme spec in an ever memeier way if thats how you have fun in the game. But if you ask for any change, the first question should always be, how can this be used to hurt/break something.

Edit:
Dont get me wrong, id love some melee moonkin shenannegans, but the supporting spells to make such a playstile actually worthy of getting extra talent support is just not there. As soon as you buff something to officially endorse it, you have a lot of people who will not see it as supporting a meme specc and actually just rant that their favorite playstile got some support but not enough. author: Tarsis
subject: ECLIPSE... WHY ?
content_md:
I have always liked druids, from D&D to Warcraft 3 and when Blizzard released WoW... well... i immediately made a Balance Druid and i kept playing it until Blizzard fucked it up and ruined it with ECLIPSE...

Eclipse is the definition of "ADDING COMPLEXITY FOR COMPLEXITY SAKE"...
It doesn't make playing the class more enjoyable, it doesn't add "flavor" to the class, it doesn't add flexibility to your playstyle, it adds constrictions and more buttons to press in a specific order, or you will perform WORST than before...

Eclipse is a NERF disguised as a BUFF.

Before i take my pants down to dump on Eclipse, let me say that the class update has been REALLY GOOD.

I was especially impressed by the Destruction Lock changes, they did a great job with it, removing Shadow Bolt from the fire spec, making Soul Fire and Searing Pain viable, they understood that if someone plays destruction, he probably wants to shoot Fire shit to enemies and not Shadow, WELL DONE.

I have many more compliments about the changes (and few eyebrow raising stuff too), but this is the Druid forum and i want to talk about Eclipse so... why is Eclipse bad?

Well to put it simple, Eclipse is a chore that penalizes you if you ignore it; is like having to dust your house or take out the garbage.

Plus all of this:

- Every other class got their damage improved, but Balance (in order to keep up with the others) has to rely on a short time buff window that triggers on a randomly generated spell crit...

- If you have to dps at specific moments during the fight, or you want to use some damage boost items, you have to cross your fingers and pray to the RNG gods for their favor, and they are shitty gods...

- If you are victim of a CC during your DPS window, you loose big DPS.

- If your target is Immune/heavy resistant to one of your two schools, you loose big DPS.

- If you have to move around during your DPS window, you loose big DPS.

- If you make a mistake and screw up your rotation, you loose big DPS.

- Forcing a class that already struggles with mana issues, to use more spells in the rotation, is sadistic.

- Gear Restrictions: forcing us to use both Nature and Arcane damage in the rotation prohibit us from using those items that buff Nature/Arcane specifically.

- PvP NERF: well is pretty obvious, if you want to heal and is not arcane damage boost time your opponent doesn't have to choose between interrupting your damage or wait for your heal/cc to go off, he just interrupts your nature school and you are stuck with the arcane school that now does 30% less damage (because remember every other class got buffed) FUN.

- TOO MUCH SHIT TO FOLLOW ON SCREEN: the Druid already has a shit ton of buttons to remember in PvP (normal spells plus Bear & Cat abilities, items, consumables, etc...) plus you have to track all other players around, enemies that need cc, allies that could use a heal or mana, and NOW i also have to constantly check which eclipse i'm on and how long does it lasts...
Now, you might be a 16yo Korean pro gamer, but i'm an old fuck with a job that doesn't have the brain capacity to process all that after 10 hours of work.
 ***ECLIPSE... My Assessment? UMGAK.***

There are many other ways to boost Druids, just on top of head, you can give us a Trent pet (or Furbolg, or whatever):

- Base abilities: Wrath (1.5 sec cast), Healing Touch (2 sec cast), no mana cost, 5 sec CD on both.

- The pet benefits of 1/3 of the owner Stats like HP, Armor, Spell DMG/Heal, 100% of owner crit/hit.
The pet has 3 fighting stances that can be swapped OUTSIDE of combat:
- Melee Stance: gains HP, Armor, Att Speed boost, a pet like Taunt, and a Gorilla pet like Stomp.

- Caster Stance: No CD on Wrath.

- Healer Stance: No CD on Healing Touch
Than just replace Eclipse with talents that gives Balance Druid 3 Treants but weaker, or the one Treant gets stronger.

Or whatever you feel like, almost anything is better than Eclipse.

I really love this server, everything you did with the world and the classes (you did a much better job than those idiots that sits inside the Blizzard building right now) and i would love to play my favorite class and have fun with it on Turtle WoW.

So i politely ask to PLZ reconsider the ECLIPSE talent for the Balance Druid.

I hope that this post reaches the devs and convince them to rethink the Eclipse introduction, or maybe you guys disagree with me and your vision of Balance Druid is completely different, and if that's the case well i will have to find a way to deal with that.

 **I wish everyone a nice day, peace.**

author: Halfgeek9
subject: Re: ECLIPSE... WHY ?
content_md:
Balance Druid DPS is bottom of the DPS tier. So the idea that its rewarding to play a spec that is more complex than other casters, with low crit chance built into the kit, that is reliant on crit rate to even function or synergize, is just flat out wrong.

It achieved more complexity, yes, but its not more rewarding. Its literally bottom of the barrel, not even mediocre.

Elemental Shaman at least has +11% crit chance to their main dmg spell, and a on demand crit ability so they can proc -mana talents when spells crit. This is synergy of design.

Druid gets -0.5s faster spell cast on crit, and the new Eclipse buff on crit, but get no crit bonuses to Wrath or Starfire, the spells that benefit from their talents when they crit.

I don't mind Eclipse, it is what it is. But the glaring lack of thought into how it plays, how it talent spec for spell crit effects but lacks bonuses to crit rate is just stupid.

Exactly, they ONLY look at raid charts and ignore EVERYTHING else.
Mob killing in open world, they die too fast to fully benefit from Eclipse, and when you move from one mob to another you waste precious seconds on you damage window, basically you spend the majority of your time with a -30% damage debuff in open world.

Reality is that Eclipse is a NERF disguised as BUFF...

Blizzard spent MANY years and multiple expansions trying to fix Eclipse and they FAILED MISERABLY...
They changed it, than changed it back, they removed the random activation, than they made that you have to use 2 consecutive Warath/Moonfire to trigger it, than they added more mechanics into it (Astral Power) trying to mitigate the fact that you have little control to when do damage, they HAD to add a CD ability that triggers BOTH ECLIPSES at the same time so you can use the spells that MAKE SENSE TO USE...

Eclipse takes away agency from you, forces you to use the wrong spell until you get a proc, so than you can use the correct spell...

IS A FUCKING MESS, in retail WoW you have to watch 7 minute guides just to understand how the fucking rotation works...

They pigeon hole themselves into this fucking HORRIBLE mechanic and stubbornly stick to it, to the point that they cant fix it nor get rid of it anymore...

DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE

Look at that mess and find another way to improve Balance Druid.

author: Tarsis
subject: Re: Leveling as balance
content_md:
Well cat is not "better" is faster/efficient: kill 2-3 normal mobs quick, self heal, than cat again and repeat, very efficient BUT you struggle vs Elite mobs due to your low mana pool.

Moonkin for me is the most enjoyable to level, because as long as your enemy is not immune to Entangling Roots, he is dead.

So my suggestions are:
- early game (until you past lvl 20 if you get some good gear) will be: hot yourself and fight in bear, if you go in dungeons you can easily dps/heal or even tank depending on your gear quality

- pick any talent that saves/restore your mana

- 2 + enemies: root any melee and wither them with dots while you kill the others

- dont strees about leather gear, pick anything with int/spirit

- don't worry about "Vengeance" or "Nature's Reach" for now (you will respec at 60)

- i suggest only 1 talent in "Owlkin Frenzy", you just want the mana regen, you dont want to cast in melee anyway

- after you took all the talents you want from the "Moonkin Form" row, i suggest to go resto to take the 15% mana regen while casting, you should have quite a lot of spirit from gear by then

- if you like alchemy, mana potions are good to always have at hand, but whatever profession you feel like is fine.
So be mindful with your mana, ROOT anything that moves and enjoy your ABSOLUTE dominance over any NPC.

Bleeds got buffed because bleeds sucked. You have 4 dps buttons that are even worth considering as a cat druid. Shred, rake, rip & bite.
 2 of which, rake and rip with their original scaling are never even useful outside of some pvp against very heavily armored classes. Just making bleed an option is a big win since it expands the depth of feral, the class that is at any moment in combat limited to the fewest amount of potentially useful buttons for a situation. You have the options for many more different situations than other classes, but even a perfectly shifting feral in classic only ever pressed 3 buttons in a fight.

Do actually integrating bleeds into ferals dps rotation deepens the skill expression of all druids.

where i dont understand the balancing of ferals is with people pretending powershfting and bleed somehow dont mix. Which couldnt be further from the truth. You get the choice between more energy or not having more energy.
So unless we have talents that reward you for staying in cat form and discourage powershifting, there is no alternate playstile. Its just playing druid at max powerlevel or not doing so

subject: Cat bleed build and bleed immunities inconsistency
content_md:
Hello everyone

I started to play on the new SA server after reading the changes to feral druid, **IMO** i feel like the need to powershift to be able to compete in the damage meters is kinda retarded and its just a bad gimmick in general. I want to get out of the form to heal people, innervate others and use my mana to better help the raid while also being able to play the way the devs wanted to. (I don't want it to be TOP DPS, but just be able to play my build in general, more on this below)

keeping up Bleeds, Tiger's Fury sounded fun to me, so I leveled from day 1 with this build in mind.

The leveling experience was great, could do some decent multi targeting bleeds, the buffs to energy seems good, just top notch experience overall.

The problem now started on the end game, level 60 DGS many mobs have bleed immunities, and they aren't consistent. Some beasts where immune (giant worm in Kara and others), some undead could bleed, some didn't, and even spirits... and tbh, it felt bad, not only because i was spending points into a build that couldn't work, but because of mob immunities inconsistency in general.

My suggestion is either make so cat bleed are a different kinda of bleed (strong bleeds) or just make it so mobs can bleed in general, or just making immunities more consistent would already feel better tbh....

Also, Ferocious Bite energy to damage feels bad, removing this effect and making it so it refreshes RIP duration would feel much better.

author: Rmoruser
subject: Re: Cat bleed build and bleed immunities inconsistency
content_md:
Bleed/Shred Cat is decent with the right gear and talents.

The Bleed talents that generate additional energy combined with Idol of Laceration (which gives your finishing moves a 20% chance per combo point to refund 15 Energy on your next Shred) allow a rotation of Rake + Shred + Rip to deliver a fairly good and consistent DPS. However, several problems make this hard to realize:

 1. Many mobs, as others have pointed out, are immune to bleed effects.

 2. In raids, bleeds become almost useless because, even if you manage to apply them, with so many debuffs on the target it’s simply impossible to track and keep your rotation going. Other players applying their own debuffs or warriors’ Wounds effects constantly overwrite and remove your bleeds. You can’t keep bleeds on the boss, so the bleed talents and their energy regeneration become ineffective.

 3. Ferals lose a significant amount of damage to glancing blows. Watching just 10 seconds of a raid fight, you’ll see many glancing hits. It would be great if ferals had a unique skill to reduce or remove glancing hits or if weapon skills could influence this.

 4.AoE damage is weak for ferals. You can always use Swipe in bear form, but if you’re not a tank, it’s pretty useless because you can’t generate enough rage to make it effective. Also, ferals don’t have the spell power needed to be effective with Hurricane on packs, and leaving cat form to do AoE just isn’t true feral gameplay.

Suggestions to improve feral gameplay:

 1)To make the bleed spec playable, bleed talents should allow bleeds to bypass bleed immunity, similar to the Hunter talent "Stinging Nettle." I believe this effect could be added exclusively to the feral cat DPS bleed talents.

 2) To solve the second issue and give bleeds a better chance to generate energy, I believe ferals need a talent that applies a Rake-like bleed effect automatically—similar to Warrior’s Wounds. Critical hits with Shred or Claw would apply this bleed to the target. This would also combine well with the earlier suggestion to let bleeds bypass immunity via bleed-specific talents. The bleed would restore energy as Rake currently does, allowing cat DPS to focus on building combo points and maintaining their Claw/Shred + Rip/Ferocious Bite rotation, while providing a more reliable source of energy regeneration during raids.

 3)In long fights (cats can’t jump higher than their own heads), it’s not uncommon to see a less-geared warrior out-DPS a feral druid in the last 20% of the encounter.

Almost every class has burst skill with cooldowns on a 2–3 minute timer, while Berserk is a 6-minute cooldown. For example, in Molten Core or Blackwing Lair, I can’t use Berserk on every boss, while other classes can use their burst on nearly every pull.

First: Please address the issue of glancing blows for ferals. On some bosses, cat DPS ends up being equal to bear DPS, which feels unrewarding for a spec focused on melee damage.

Second: Consider splitting Berserk into two separate abilities — one for bear form and one for cat form. A 6-minute cooldown is acceptable for a tanking defensive ability, but it's far too long for DPS. Reducing the cat version of Berserk to 3 minutes (like Warrior’s Death Wish) would make it more viable in raid environments. Alternatively, you could introduce a talent that reduces Berserk’s cooldown by 1–2 seconds per critical hit.

Also worth noting: Berserk only increases energy regeneration and doesn’t directly boost abilitys damage or white attacks. This means that even during Berserk, druids remain limited by energy regeneration, stats, and the global cooldown.

 4)It’s pretty sad that Raka’shishi, Spear of the Adrift Hunt’s effect doesn’t work for druids. Warriors and Hunters are already top AoE classes, so this weapon ends up situationally useful for Warriors and very strong for Hunters. I’m not sure if Paladins would bother picking it up for DPS just to get extra damage on the closest target once every 5 seconds, since it doesn’t increase damage to the primary target compared to other weapons.
Why doesn’t it work for druids? Is it because druids’ melee attacks hit harder than other classes wielding weapons?

It would be great if this effect also worked for ferals (anyway it’s limited by cooldown), or would be nice to have a cat version of Swipe to dont  leave cat form to cast Hurricane or switch to bear form. Even then, it’s mostly ineffective because cats aren’t tanks and don’t generate enough rage.
