author: Rmoruser
subject: Re: Cat bleed build and bleed immunities inconsistency
content_md:
1. As i understood  "Stinging Nettle" is fine.

Your Mongoose Bite and triggered Fire traps now apply your highest rank of Serpent Sting for 40% of the duration. Serpent Stings applied this way ignore resistances and immunities.

Fire traps and melee skill applied range skill(nature) and ignore 2 mechanics resistance and immunities.

My suggestion is to add bleed ignore to the bleed spec. (It just makes more sense to me than the hunter’s Stinging Nettle.) Anyway, you won’t be dealing more damage than you’re actually capable of.

Also, this will mainly be useful only at longer ranges — because on trash mobs with low HP, Shred/Ferocious Bite will still be more effective.

 2. Yes, Ancient Brutality is insane, especially with Idol of Laceration. But if almost everything is immune to bleed, it becomes ineffective. Although for tanks it works well because it relies on dodge mechanics, not on the fact that almost every mob/boss, especially in endgame, has immunity to bleed.

About Swipe: yeah, you can spam Swipe in bear form. Rage-wise — sure, you’ll have enough for nonstop Swipe action, but your damage is capped by the skill itself and the fact that Swipe only hits up to three targets. Meanwhile, you won’t really be able to use Maul or Savage Bite effectively (except clearcast procs). Honestly, I think even a rank 1 Arcane Explosion mage could out-DPS you here.

As a result, your overall DPS will be lower than the tank’s, who gets enough rage regeneration to spam all their skills non-stop — unlike you. That’s why, when facing big packs, Hurricane ends up being a bit more effective.

Sorry, but we’re not talking about top-tier game DPS here. Mages and Warriors are still kings when it comes to both single-target and AoE damage.

So, my suggestion is simply to make druids happy by letting them do decent DPS — not top-tier, just normal and playable, based on their talents and spec. If you’re a bleed specialization, then it makes sense for bleeds to be applied properly.

Let’s also take a look at Tier 2.5:

(5) Set Bonus: Damage of your Rake and Rip have a 6% and 10% chance respectively to empower your next Shred, Rip, or Claw, increasing its critical strike chance and damage by 15%.

It literally says your Shred is empowered by your bleed effects — but once again, in the next endgame raids (naxx,kara40), this becomes nearly useless since almost everything is immune to bleeds.

This bonus would’ve made much more sense on Tier 1, where bleeds are actually usable — for example, when farming BWL or AQ40.

Now take the Tier 1 (8) Set Bonus:

Ferocious Bite has a 20% chance per combo point spent to put you into a frenzy, increasing the attack speed of your next 5 attacks by 15%.

That one would actually make more sense on Tier 2.5, since in endgame content you’re using Shred and Ferocious Bite much more frequently due to bleed immunities.

Sure, you’re probably not going to use the full 5/5 Tier 2.5 bonus anyway —
but it still feels kind of silly to have a set bonus that completely loses its effectiveness right after AQ40, simply because the next raid content is mostly bleed immune.

>  but it still feels kind of silly to have a set bonus that completely loses its effectiveness right after AQ40, simply because the next raid content is mostly bleed immune.

Idol of Laceration works with fero bite too
content_html:
1. As i understood "Stinging Nettle" is fine.

Your Mongoose Bite and triggered Fire traps now apply your highest rank of Serpent Sting for 40% of the duration. Serpent Stings applied this way ignore resistances and immunities.

Fire traps and melee skill applied range skill(nature) and ignore 2 mechanics resistance and immunities.

My suggestion is to add bleed ignore to the bleed spec. (It just makes more sense to me than the hunter’s Stinging Nettle.) Anyway, you won’t be dealing more damage than you’re actually capable of.

Also, this will mainly be useful only at longer ranges — because on trash mobs with low HP, Shred/Ferocious Bite will still be more effective.

2. Yes, Ancient Brutality is insane, especially with Idol of Laceration. But if almost everything is immune to bleed, it becomes ineffective. Although for tanks it works well because it relies on dodge mechanics, not on the fact that almost every mob/boss, especially in endgame, has immunity to bleed.

About Swipe: yeah, you can spam Swipe in bear form. Rage-wise — sure, you’ll have enough for nonstop Swipe action, but your damage is capped by the skill itself and the fact that Swipe only hits up to three targets. Meanwhile, you won’t really be able to use Maul or Savage Bite effectively (except clearcast procs). Honestly, I think even a rank 1 Arcane Explosion mage could out-DPS you here.

As a result, your overall DPS will be lower than the tank’s, who gets enough rage regeneration to spam all their skills non-stop — unlike you. That’s why, when facing big packs, Hurricane ends up being a bit more effective.

Sorry, but we’re not talking about top-tier game DPS here. Mages and Warriors are still kings when it comes to both single-target and AoE damage.

So, my suggestion is simply to make druids happy by letting them do decent DPS — not top-tier, just normal and playable, based on their talents and spec. If you’re a bleed specialization, then it makes sense for bleeds to be applied properly.

Let’s also take a look at Tier 2.5:

(5) Set Bonus: Damage of your Rake and Rip have a 6% and 10% chance respectively to empower your next Shred, Rip, or Claw, increasing its critical strike chance and damage by 15%.

It literally says your Shred is empowered by your bleed effects — but once again, in the next endgame raids (naxx,kara40), this becomes nearly useless since almost everything is immune to bleeds.

This bonus would’ve made much more sense on Tier 1, where bleeds are actually usable — for example, when farming BWL or AQ40.

Now take the Tier 1 (8) Set Bonus:

Ferocious Bite has a 20% chance per combo point spent to put you into a frenzy, increasing the attack speed of your next 5 attacks by 15%.

That one would actually make more sense on Tier 2.5, since in endgame content you’re using Shred and Ferocious Bite much more frequently due to bleed immunities.

Sure, you’re probably not going to use the full 5/5 Tier 2.5 bonus anyway —
but it still feels kind of silly to have a set bonus that completely loses its effectiveness right after AQ40, simply because the next raid content is mostly bleed immune.

subject: The way druid tier sets work is disappointing
content_md:
I'm new to druid in twow so unless I've majorly misunderstood something (which I don't think I have have), then I don't know if anyone else feels this way but honestly for me it's drove me away from playing the class...

One of my main draws to turtle wow was that all specs have become viable and with that, tier sets have been adjusted so there is mostly one available for each role a class can play. So for example, paladin has 3 roles, and now has access to 3 tier sets options for each raid tier, one for healers, one for dps and one for tanks.

For druids for some reason it just doesn't work this way. If you want to tank, you get to 60 and start running MC and realise all of the tier 1 gear is specced for a feral dps. Then tier 2 is specced towards tank druid, tier 3 also tank druid, and kara40 gear is specced for a dps druid again.

One thing that really bothers me is that I think its disheartening doing a whole raid tier and you're not going to be working towards any cool class identifying gear set. Also, kara40 just came out and the gear looks sick, and its pretty pointless to even bother collecting that if you're a druid tank. I just don't really understand the reasoning for this at all considering all of the alternative tier sets they've made for each class. I really think considering adding feral dps and feral tank sets to each tier would be welcomed and bring more people to the class...

author: Deeno
subject: Re: swift travel form questline
content_md:
Swift Travel Form

 1. 'Mount Hyjal In Turmoil' Speak with Loganaar in Moonglade and travel to Nordanaar.
 2. 'Shadowed Spectre' Archdruid Dreamwind wants you to investigate the abnormality ****west of Darkhollow Pass**** in Hyjal.
 3. 'The Son Of Cenarius' Bring 20 Brigth Dream Shards to Keeper Remulos in western Moonglade.
'4. Tethered Memories' Gather the Bough of Cenarius from Dreamstalker in Bough Shadow, Ashenvale; the Crystalline Ray of Moonlight from Venethas in a cave north of Everlook, Winterspring; and the Jade Scale of the Dreamer from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum raid for Keeper Remulos.
 5. 'The White Stag' Return to the Spectre west of Darkhollow Pass and defeat it, return to Keeper Remulos afterwards.
 6. 'Woven Dreams' Gather 10 Viridian Mushrooms from Jademir Lake in Feralas, as well as other materials for Keeper Remulos.
 7. 'The Eternal Sleeper' Travel to Seradane in the Hinterlands and convene with the spirit of Vithekus.
 8. 'Under the Vibrant Moonlight' Gather friends in the Twilight Grove of Duskwood and receive the blessing as your reward.

author: Slade1994
subject: Cat Powershifting
content_md:
Hey team, I am a cat player from SEA server.

Just wanted to bring up an issue that’s been affecting Feral (Cat) Druids on Turtle WoW — and it’s something that was actually confirmed and fixed by Blizzard during TBC Classic.

Right now, energy regen for Cat Form is bugged: if you shapeshift right before a 2-second energy tick (like at 1.9s), the regen timer resets and you lose that tick entirely. Over the course of a fight, that’s a huge DPS loss.

This isn’t how it’s supposed to work. By design, Cats should get 40 Energy on shift and then 20 Energy every 2 seconds, regardless of when the shift happens. Blizzard acknowledged this exact problem in TBC Classic and pushed out a fix — after that, shifting no longer reset the tick timer. You’d still get your energy right on time, even if you shifted just before the tick.

Players even found workarounds back then (like using Troll’s Blood Elixir to “trick” the timer), but obviously that’s not sustainable or intended.

Can we please get this fixed on Turtle WoW too? It’s a confirmed bug with a known solution. Feral DPS already struggles in some areas — we don’t need bugs making it worse.

Thanks!

I have linked the reference below.

[https://www.bluetracker.gg/wow/topic/us ... e-28-2021/](https://www.bluetracker.gg/wow/topic/us-en/23646890-hotfixes-june-28-2021/)

[https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t ... te/1008243](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/t/feral-druid-update/1008243)

author: Forumdweller
subject: Make Druid a proper hybrid once and for all
content_md:
Druid was my first ever class and I mained it since I first got introduced to the game by a family member back in 2006.
Back then in my eyes the Druid was a versatile class that can perform any function and had access to tools that nobody else did. I wasn't a feral, balance, or healer druid. I was just a druid that could adapt on the go with the many baseline tools I had at my disposal. This is quite a farcry from what the Druid class currently is, and I know that it's both a massive change to what we have currently have and on the extreme end of the never going to happen on Turtle spectrum. But I haven't enjoyed this class since mop (after the novelty wore off) and if this inspires even one person to open their mind to the possibilities of this class then I will have succeeded. Here's what I propose.

The existing no cooldown stance system needs to be changed. Forms should not operate in the exact same fashion that warrior stances do.  Instead they'll be extremely powerful buffs that last no longer than 10 seconds and tied to long cooldowns. They wont turn you into animals anymore either, but they'll provide various visual cues depending on the inhabited stance similar to this guy in LoL (no I don't play it). <https://gyazo.com/dafecf65ced84c6c880f06d5ac7f6e22>

Want to use bear abilities? Activate bear stance, grow enormous oversized paws (as a human/nelf whatever) and slap people to death.

Follow the same logic with cat (being a fast, reflexive stance that can dodge attacks)

strengthen your connection to the stars temporarily and become attuned to astral magics for a short duration with long ranged attacks and aoe damage

This encourages the 'not a feral, balance nor a resto druid' mentality that was intended with the OG druid. You're just a HUMANOID druid that can temporarily take on the aspects of various beasts.

I tried leveling as moonkin but it's so damn boring, no amount of 'go oom' slower talents are going to make this enjoyable. What's enjoyable for me is being versatile, dotting everything up, kiting them around while I rejuvenate and cleanse myself of poisons and diseases and weaving auto attacks in between. Not the boring spam wrath and moonfire as a fat abomination chicken that balance has become.

Again, not going to happen but atleast it's out there now and hopefully someone who cares about this classes identity sees it and does something with it, however insignificant.

It's been over 20 years since druid was released and nothing innovative has happened with this class. I think it has went backwards. If blizzard had the tools we have today back then I think druid would be much closer to the vision I'm creating above. They wouldnt've just made them specialize in 1 form like we have now. Atleast go all the way and make it a fun class like they have in TWW where they cast super fast and summon trees and faerie dragons and melt everything around them. Right now its like you've just went 5% of the way (in the wrong direction) and given up.

Sucks because I know that you guys are really capable of achieving something amazing like you've already done with the custom pve content in the form of dungeons, zones, music.

author: Quetzy
subject: Re: Make Druid a proper hybrid once and for all
content_md:
I’m fully in favor of bringing back the hybrid identity of the druid (and other hybrid classes too). One of the great things about original WoW design was the flexibility to adapt and fill in where needed, instead of being locked into rigid roles.

The issue isn’t that hybrid gameplay doesn’t work — it’s that the current group-building and role system is completely closed off. When forming a party, you’re forced to choose one of the “holy trinity” roles: tank, healer, or DPS. There’s no real option for a hybrid role, or for dynamic party compositions.

But the reality is, most dungeons (outside of raids) could easily be completed with more creative setups, such as:

Two druids who both heal and contribute damage.

Two tanks who share pulls and rotate mitigation.

Groups with no pure healer, but several classes sharing utility healing and support.

These kinds of comps actually worked back in Vanilla, but over time they've been sidelined by modern expectations and rigid role tools — even on old-school servers like Turtle WoW.

Reviving the druid’s hybrid playstyle wouldn’t just be true to the class fantasy — it would actually enhance gameplay. It would promote creativity in group composition, reduce the “LF healer/tank” bottleneck, and make content more approachable for non-meta builds.

author: Cheruscan
subject: Re: Make Druid a proper hybrid once and for all
content_md:
I think the idea is novel and I especially vibe with the not-always-shapeshited idea, I put alot of care creating my characters so I dont want to hide them turning into a bear all the time or becoming a colored ghost.

However making a jack-of-all-trades/master of none just wont do outside of a friend group that tolerates it.

I play in a casual raiding guild and specific Naxx bosses and our first dips into Kara40 have shown that there is a limit to casual play. Its ok if somebody fail the first 3 times on an encounter but after that it just becomes frustrating, especially if their failings make us wipe which costs time and gold of every raider.

Now image if druids just couldnt compete at all due to hybrid tax so even a skilled player would just troll the whole raid in essence.

I bring up raiding because this would be the only form of content this hybrid beast idea would just not fit in.

Druids in PvP already mix in pieces (mostly weapons since you can switch those in combat) from different speccs to make their heals or dmg spells pop more while constantly switching between caster and bear form to mitigate incoming dmg.

Dungeons are also free game unless you have a freshly dinged 60 group that decides going SW Vault in full greens is a smart idea.

The only versatility role I can think of that would also be viable for raiding would be a mixture of restoration and balance occupying a similar space to shadowpriest OR a melee support specc that focuses on buffs and reducing incoming dmg of group members with mechanics similar to the sublety rogue but with more active mitigation (like how warriors intervene works) were you switch between bear for active mitigation/buffs in the form of roars and cat form for debuffs (expose weakness esque stuff)

Gotta mention that you can just aswell RP this melee support playstyle with a nelf subtlety rogue that uses fist weapons (without the active, intervene style, mitigation ofc)

author: Justbe
subject: Allow Genesis to effect bleed dots as well
content_md:
Druids are my favourite class, bar none.

When I saw genesis added to the game and that it increased damage over time abilities the wheels started turning on how I could level a new way that would be unique and would allow me to use more of my kit.

Then one of the devs on discord told me that genesis only worked with magical damage over time abilities, meaning bleeds were not affected, I was completely disheartened.

I would love if genesis would apply to bleed effects as well. A leveling rotation for this was extremely fun and satisfying applying dots to multiple enemies and watching them all melt while you kept yourself topped off.

I don't even believe this would change much in terms of the end game, as genesis is so far down the resto tree no feral dps would go that far just for a small increase in bleed damage.

Was this ever tested? What is the rational behind not allowing Genesis to apply to bleed effects.

Please make this happen as it would give druids an extremely fun, different way to level that was boomkin or 100% uptime cat form.

author: Quetzy
subject: Suggestion: Mounted-Speed Travel Form
content_md:
I really appreciate the addition of the improved Travel Form that counts as a mount — it’s a great step toward making the druid feel more unique and connected to nature.

That said, I’d like to propose an idea that could take this even further while staying true to the druid’s fantasy and class identity.

What if, once the player learns the level 40 riding skill, the druid could unlock an upgraded version of Travel Form through a class-specific quest? This form would:

Only be usable out of combat

Require a short cast time (just like a mount)

Move at standard mount speed

Keep the flavor and immersion of shapeshifting instead of summoning a mount

This would allow druids to remain in form — enhancing the fantasy of being a creature of nature — while not breaking the game balance, since it would functionally act like a mount with the same limitations.

There are many ways this could be implemented:

A druid-only quest involving natural spirits or wild zones

A learned skill only usable in Travel Form at level 40 if you’ve learned riding

A talent path exclusive to the class

I think it’s a great opportunity to reinforce the uniqueness of the druid, and give players a more immersive alternative to traditional mounts — without giving them any unfair mechanical advantage.

Would love to hear what others think!

author: Profgiggles
subject: Re: Maximum speed
content_md: Speed buffs never stack. If you have more than one speed buff active, the higher value buff is the active one. 100% speed is your default movement speed. Feral swiftness brings you up to 130%. Dash or swiftness potion takes you up to 150%. Using dash + swiftness potion will still have you moving at 150% speed, however you can use a swiftness potion after your dash runs out to prolong your speed buff.

author: Decavi
subject: Suggestion: Feral Druid Tier Set Rework
content_md:
Hello,

I’d like to propose a rework or reconsideration of the itemization on Feral Druid tier sets. As it currently stands, it feels highly inefficient — and honestly, disappointing — to see so much Intellect on gear that is supposed to be tailored for Feral Druids, especially when it's intended for tanking or melee DPS roles.

Intellect is largely a wasted stat on Feral Druids. Even if the justification is to support shapeshifting with a larger mana pool, having 100+ Intellect on a set that is meant for a form that doesn’t use mana or cast spells feels excessive and impractical. A much better approach would be to replace Intellect with useful offensive (Strength, Crit, Hit) or defensive (Stamina, Armor, Defense) stats.

It’s also strange that main tank sets (like T2 and T3) are given to Feral Druids when, in most cases, non-set pieces with the right stat distribution are far superior for bear tanking. On the other hand, Feral DPS Druids get Tier 2.5, which is ironically outclassed by other loot in the same raid. And yes, those other pieces often don’t carry Intellect — making them more viable for Feral builds.

The newly introduced Tier 3.5 (from Kara40) seems to fall into the same trap: it gives around 120+ Intellect, again, on a class/spec that does not use mana nor spells in combat. I believe most players would agree — it makes as little sense as giving Intellect to a Rogue.

It’s unfortunate to see such a unique and flavorful spec like Feral being overlooked or misrepresented in itemization. I hope this suggestion can serve as constructive feedback and encourage a more tailored approach in future tier designs.

Thank you for your time, and for all the hard work on Turtle WoW.

subject: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
Druids deserve a base resurrection spell. I understand that they did not have a revive ability in vanilla. But this is vanilla+ and the whole point is to correct all the mistakes and design flaws of the original rushed, unfinished game that is classic vanilla.

All tank classes should have access to a taunt ability and all healer classes should have access to an out of combat resurrection ability--period. There's no debate to be had. These spells are integral to the identity of their respective roles. Tanks taunt, healers heal and revive fallen comrades.

author: Sandrex
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
I periodically return to the turtle project, and the first thing I ask the players is - have the developers added resurrection for the druid?
So, what is a druid? It is an easy and convenient leveling up to level 60, and then - deletion. Because in the raid there are only 2 (and sometimes only 1) slots for a druid. A tank and a cat are a difficult and tedious path to getting good equipment at the middle stage of the game, and only if you are in a good guild. Well, for a tank it is easier to do this because of the eternal shortage of tanks in the dungeons.
And a healer needs to visit many high-level dungeons to get pre-raid equipment. But often when choosing a group, a druid is simply NOT TAKEN, refusing for various reasons. What can I say, when I myself assemble a group, I choose a healer from shamans / paladins / priests. Experienced players understand that in BRD or higher, where you can die by accidentally capturing an extra mob, resurrection is a must have.
Giving the druid a normal resurrection without a cooldown is an obvious and correct decision, it is unclear why the developers do not want to do this.

author: Lordmarrowgar
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
I'm on the opposite side of this request. Why?
 - Players often call for more immersion with class-specific experiences, and i agree wholeheartedly.

In raids (and likely dungeons too), we usually have 1 or more paladins or Priests in the group. Why not use their ability to resurrect fallen players out of combat? Combat resurrection is where druids truly shine.

Based on years of experience as a healer, I know some might disagree, but:
 - Druid healers are the MVPs for emergency healing, thanks to instant casts like Swiftmend (15s cooldown), and the instant cast HoT's.
 - They have major mobility compared to other healers.
 - Vanilla dungeons and raids feel slow because many players make them so with a classic mindset.

My 2 cent,:
 -If you want to boost druid healers impact, add Wild Growth, as how it was done in retail’s SoD. Or more in the style of Turtle WoW: remove the need for last-hitting to trigger Sylvan’s Blessing talent.

 -To make druids more desirable in groups, shorten the Combat Resurrection cooldown or make it cost less mana to ress with Rebirth.
 --Or, like in retail, increase their damage in healer spec. More damage means faster kills and less healing required, which might be too much of a competitive meta mindset for chilling in Turtle, but nevertheless..

But most of all:
 -Please avoid making all classes in the same like retail has done. I’ve played there for many years and watched my class(es) change into a generic framework with different colors.

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
I'm not in favor of 'samism' but I think there are certain abilities all builds from a specific role should have.
F.ex. all tanks should be able to taunt and all healers should be able to reliably rezz.
At raids, this is almost irrelevant.
But even now, that contents are made pretty easy, there are wipes in 5 man contents.
Many players are casual, pull badly, let the pet run all over the place, etc.
And having to wait 10 minutes for a corpse run every time someone did something stupid over and over again just feels punishing.
Sure, most 5 man comps have at least one priest, shaman or pala, but it is never guaranteed.
Adding a normal rez would only result in one thing:
Somewhat noob dungeon comps with f.ex. the comp of a warrior tank, a rogue, a lock, a hunter and a druid don't have to wait a lot of extra time because someone keeps corpse running from a far away graveyard.

While I understand the desire to give druids a normal resurrection, it’s important to remember why class identity matters.
Priests only got a form of battle rez through *Proclaim Champion* — a 2-hour cooldown, restricted to the chosen champion, and locked deep in their talent tree. Druids, on the other hand, have a much shorter cooldown and can use it on anyone. That difference is part of what made their utility unique.

Yes, WotLK eventually added a standard resurrection for druids, but here we are in Vanilla+ because we value preserving the spirit of Classic. Bringing in changes from later expansions step-by-step moves us away from what makes this version special and towards retail-style homogenization.

Improving the game doesn’t have to mean erasing the differences that make each class interesting.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
> **Akos1896 wrote: Tue Aug 12, 2025 9:44 am**
> I'm not in favor of 'samism' but I think there are certain abilities all builds from a specific role should have.
>  F.ex. all tanks should be able to taunt and all healers should be able to reliably rezz.
>  At raids, this is almost irrelevant.
>  But even now, that contents are made pretty easy, there are wipes in 5 man contents.
>  Many players are casual, pull badly, let the pet run all over the place, etc.
>  And having to wait 10 minutes for a corpse run every time someone did something stupid over and over again just feels punishing.
>  Sure, most 5 man comps have at least one priest, shaman or pala, but it is never guaranteed.
>  Adding a normal rez would only result in one thing:
>  Somewhat noob dungeon comps with f.ex. the comp of a warrior tank, a rogue, a lock, a hunter and a druid don't have to wait a lot of extra time because someone keeps corpse running from a far away graveyard.

I understand the argument that “all healers should be able to rez,” but that mixes two completely different concepts:
 - Abilities essential for a class to perform its *core role in combat* (like taunt for tanks)
 - Out-of-combat convenience tools that are not required for the role to function during the fight

A druid’s battle rez is actually far more impactful than a normal resurrection — it can turn a wipe into a kill mid-fight, which is far more valuable than simply skipping a corpse run afterwards.

In retail, Blizzard added mass resurrection because “it’s out of combat, so why not make it easy for everyone?” The result was that corpse runs became trivial and death lost part of its intended penalty.

Death in WoW, especially in Vanilla+, is meant to have consequences.
Corpse running forces players to slow down, regroup, and recover — it’s a moment where mistakes are acknowledged, and the entire group shares responsibility for keeping each other alive. If someone dies far from the graveyard, it should feel like a setback, not just a minor pause while someone presses a button.

Adding a standard rez to druids would not fix a broken mechanic — it would only make certain dungeon runs slightly faster when no other rezzer is present. The game is designed so that not every possible party combination can ignore that downtime, and that’s part of the intended challenge.

subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
I think it’s a good idea to put it somewhere in the talents so that lvl 24-25 healing druids could get a res. I think it’s a great idea someone posted earlier.

If I’m being honest, if I were a healing Druid in raids, I wouldn’t want to have a res spell at all. Rezzing the dead is so braindead and you are very likely to miss the pull while you res, I’m saying this as someone who plays priest. So I completely understand raiding resto Druids not wanting to engage in this mess. We can’t be disingenuous and deny that it can be a huge reason why druids would say no. Because it’s just boring.

But from the perspective of a healing Druid who heals 5 man, res is very important. Imagine being in a group with no paladin (which is hard to imagine on turtle, I know, but let’s try). You are indeed in a very weird position and I’m sure people have been rejected as healing druids from low lvl content because there were no resser in the group.

So we have raiding druids vs dungeoning druids. It’s a bit disingenuous that no one mentions a more practical and pragmatic reason why they wouldn’t want to have a full on res spell. Diversity va homogenisation, ok, sounds great in theory. But having no res spell while doing dead mines and making your group mates corpse walk?

But I wouldn’t be surprised if there were even devs who are raiding druids who realistically just don’t want to do this braindead labour and that’s why they are not going to add it. Like we can add so many things from wotlk but not Druid res? Is there a more real reason why besides homogenisation? Shadow priests now have aoe too, so. I don’t understand when this argument ends.

subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
I see no need for an ooc res. And I say that as a druid main who levelled up as a dungeon healer using Slow & Steady.

If you want to play around an ooc res, play any of the other 3 healers. Not everyone is supposed to be great at everything, that's the charm of picking a class. Yes, no ooc res is a major inconvenience. And playing around it contributes to making druid a unique and fun experience.

I'm not categorically opposed, but it would probably be yet another step in the wrong direction in terms of class changes and class balance. If anything we should be looking to tone down the whacky CC powercreep, not further it.

> Nah, helps build character and better dps

This deserves to be highlighted. WoW is supposed to have difficulty. Group composition and player skill are supposed to matter. CC2 overtuned numbers so much, that the general expectation is just to faceroll dungeons. But you're supposed to take it slowly and methodically, use your tools. Tanks are supposed to hold aggro. author: Templar85
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
Nice to see more veteran druids joined the conversation. However in this case I not agree with them that druids don't need rez.

Need deeper understanding of the problem.
- I don't want ress because it is boring and not fun
It is a global problem for every healer class that resurrection time is  10 seconds. The origin of 10 seconds came from pre alpha development idea. Devs told originally they choose 10 seconds because they envisioned it cam be used in combat too. They don't wanted to be op, so set it to 10 seconds. Later they scraped the idea that every healer can use it in combat, but the timer for some reason stayed for 10 seconds.

In 2025 there is no reason that it should stay that long. Reduction to 5 seconds more reasonable. There are ways to punish player who dies too often. Currently ressing a dead player punishing the healer with a 10 seconds spell. Shorter ress time may incentivize players to be more reckless and not cautious enough but there are better ways to counter balance this

There can be more gold penalty or their abilities doing x% less damage if death occurred in a short period of time.
Another way is healer just need to initiate the spell but don't need to channel it for the duration. The player still have to wait 10 seconds to be alive.

Conclusion: There are many creative ways to handle this situation. Not every vanilla thing was good that worth to keep. Understanding the motives behind an ability and having a clear focus what behavior we intending to players is the key. We have the Zul gurub set that reduces Br by 10 mins but like I told many times fixing Duid core toolkit problems should not amend by gear rather by talent design.

- Homogenatization
This can be a rubber bone or a tool for disqualification method for other player made suggestion which "I don't like" in conversation or can be a real valid point. In my opinion Turtle is miles and miles away in class design wise to that end. Because they were very conservative they can make like 100 more changes and still we will be far from a relative "omg every class is homogenized now" standpoint.

- Dungeons are too easy now if druid can ressurect. There is no CC required anymore
Instead of negating a healer class a key ability maybe make dungeons more harder by giving more mechanics to them?
Although this is a deeper subject. I advocated for a very long time that for a hard dungeon specifically for T3 geared players. Can flavor it with many random elements so it will be not just another boring stomp fest.

- "But battle ress is super op spell that can turn the battle if used correctly"
With a 30 minute timer this is a HUGE restriction to be used as often and be an OP spell. What happens if 2 people dies but I can battleress one? Group still need to wait for the other player. He/she might pull a mob or patrol beck in the way and die again. Keep separating group members cause friction and annoyance. Tank says I don't have time to wait until dead player running back for 5-10 mins and leaving. This is not happening with a healer who have normal resurrection.

- Druid long cd spells like Battle ress and Tranquility can have high impact in a raid environment (if used the right time) but for dungeons it is extremely restricted because of the long CD.
Paladins and Warriors have talents to reduce their long CD abilities. Pala Improved Lay on Hands talent and Warriors Improved Discipline and Improved Shield Wall talents.

My Ideas for long CD spells should be more often used in a not 40 player environment and support it with ability, talent changes:
- IF druid used Battleress or Tranq in a dungeon(or affected max 15 people) then cd time will be 15 mins instead of 30.

- New talent in Balance tree. Tranq cd set to 15 mins but half as much healing output and for compensation Battle Ress gain a second charge dungeon only.

- Effective healing reduces BR CD. For X amount of effective heal x seconds taken away from the cd

- After X amount of effective healing druids earns a normal resurrection spell for 30 mins. Can stack up to 3 charges.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
You seem to be missing the key trade-off here.
Druids have *battle rez* at the cost of not having a baseline out-of-combat rez. That’s the balance. Battle rez is fight-saving and available to all specs — not just a convenience spell after combat.

To address your points:

 **“Priests and druids too alike”** – My comparison wasn’t about making them identical, but about the fact that priest’s *Proclaim Champion* is a far more limited version of battle rez. Druids can use theirs on anyone, with a much shorter cooldown in practical terms, and without talent-tree restrictions.

 **Cooldown length** – Yes, in absolute numbers it’s not “short,” but considering its power — bringing someone back mid-fight — it’s an extremely strong tool. Reducing that cooldown for Restoration could be a discussion, but replacing it with a normal rez removes part of the druid’s class kit identity.

 **Baseline for all healers** – Having a healer tree doesn’t mean all baseline utility should be the same. Each healer brings something different to the table:
• Paladins can DI someone at the cost of their own life, and have very fast single-target heals with excellent mana efficiency.
• Shamans have Ankh to self-rez and return to the fight, plus very strong area spells and mana-regenerating totems.
• Priests have Proclaim Champion in their talent tree — a weaker, more limited form of battle rez — but possess a very strong and diversified healing kit.
• Druids have battle rez for anyone, but no baseline out-of-combat rez, Tranquility healing that can save a raid, very strong HoTs, and solid single-target healing.

This trade-off is intentional.

Also, on this server, druids are already in a very strong spot in terms of DPS, HPS, and mitigation/threat. They don’t need an additional baseline rez to perform their role effectively.

Giving Restoration a baseline rez at the end of their tree could be a reasonable middle ground — but adding it to all druids just for convenience would be a solution in search of a problem.

Hey, nice — someone that is civilized and actually wants to keep the conversation going!

You’re mixing “universally essential” with “universally convenient.”

A taunt for a tank is essential to perform their role in combat. A standard out-of-combat rez for a healer is not — the role can be performed 100% without it.
Druids have an in-combat rez that no other healer has, and the trade-off for that is not having a baseline out-of-combat rez. That’s deliberate design, not an “error.”

If your point is “every healer must have the same tools,” then by your own logic we should also give battle rez to priests, shamans, and paladins. But we both know that would start removing the very differences that make class kits meaningful.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
At this point, I think we can agree the conversation has run its course.
We have two clear sides here:

• One group values class identity over convenience. They believe certain trade-offs, like druids having an in-combat resurrection but no baseline out-of-combat rez, are part of what makes Classic unique and should be preserved — although they admitted that adding a baseline rez to the Tree form could be an interesting compromise, without losing class identity and following the pattern of class changes already established in Turtle WoW.

• The other group sees adding a baseline resurrection to druids as a small change that would improve the game for everyone, reducing downtime without significantly impacting balance. Their main argument is that if a class can be a healer, it should have a rez, as if resurrection were an intrinsic part of every healer’s base kit — following what was done in WotLK, which is far from Classic.

Both positions have been stated and defended multiple times. Unless someone can bring a completely new perspective or argument to the table, further back-and-forth is unlikely to change minds.

author: Wilsonsds
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> Giving druid a regular rez doesn't take away the exclusiveness of having a battle rez. It's their thing still, trade-offs be damned

When you design a class, you have to think of abilities as if they cost “points.” Battle Rez is an iconic druid mechanic, and the trade-off is intentional.
I could see adding a normal rez to Restoration form, or even swapping — giving Restoration the battle rez and base druids the normal rez — but giving *both* to the base class? That’s pushing for imbalance purely for convenience.

> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> Are we fine with holy strike? Paladin had seals as a trade-off for not having a generic melee ability, didn't they? Feral druids getting berserk impedes the identity of rogue's adrenaline rush! Besides, they already have powershifting! That's the tradeoff!

Hybrid classes will inevitably share some abilities with others *in combat* — that’s part of being hybrid.
Your comparison is like asking “Why doesn’t mage have fear? Priest and warlock do.” Well, mage has frost nova and blink — those are its core combat trade-offs.
Outside of combat: mage makes water, warlock makes healthstones… should priest also get a consumable just because they’re all casters?
Or better yet — all classes can use daggers, except paladin. Should we give them daggers because “they can hold a knife”? That’s called class design. Forcing changes for convenience ruins the game.

> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> The homogenization argument blows things way out of proportion.

You’re not just removing or adding value — you’re breaking the structure these abilities were designed around.
There’s near unanimous agreement that adding a rez deep in the Restoration tree makes sense. But giving it to *all specs* breaks balance and structure.

> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> You NEED a "real" healer class present in a group to res more than one person.

Welcome to hybrid classes, my friend — they aren’t meant to have *everything*, only parts of what others have.

> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> 30 minute CD, compared to regular res spell's no CD condition.

Seriously, have you tried using a normal rez in combat? How many raids were saved by it compared to battle rez? That cooldown is the price for being able to turn a wipe into a win.

> **Bigsmerf wrote:**
> Your fear of this game turning into the slop trough that is retail WoW blinds you.

It’s not fear — it’s knowledge. I’ve seen where these “small changes” lead in the past, and I don’t want to see it happen here.

There can be arguments of convenience versus the long term health. This isn't one of them. This is one about a baseline ability for a classes roles. This would positively impact the long-term health of the game. The fact that this is even a debate is insane.

 1. Are druids a healing class? Yes.
 2. Is resurrection spells part of a healing classes baseline abilities? Yes.
 3. Does this negatively impact anyone else? No.
 4. Does this change the playstyle of the class? No, not at all.
 5. Does NOT having it negatively impact anyone? Yes, greatly.

You might not have played retail when this was a thing but I did. I played from the start of TBC till just before ICC came out in WotLK. During TBC druids were majorly hated outside of raids where others could pick up the slack from the missing utility.

When it came to 5 mans and heroics:

 1. Cat and Moonkin wasn't wanted because of the lack of crowd control and interrupts. Entangling Roots isn't usable in almost every instance so can't be counted as such. So they brought none of that and Cat form required the PvP gloves to give maim an interrupt for the fights that needed one which still took combo points and was on the global cool down unless the move was telegraphed then instead the druid could run out, shift to bear form just to feral charge back in to have an interrupt without killing their DPS as much making sure they could maim with the gloves for that encounter.

 2. Bear wasn't wanted because the difficulty in AoE threat with swipe capping out at 3 in 5 man pulls regularly. So a DPS tried to AoE, it was a crapshoot. And the lack of interrupt that warriors and blood elf paladins provided.

 3. And the Tree wasn't wanted due to this singular issue because people hated having to wait for the walk of shame every time anyone of their 5 man group died.

And these weren't just what I experienced by myself. These were automatic assumptions in Looking for Group and all with many even specifying they wanted a Warrior or Paladin tank, a Paladin, Priest or Shaman preferred Healer, and a DPS that wasn't a druid. There was even a running gag that Ghostcrawler (Developer) hated druids. Unless you ran with friends, the druid was last picked for everything in 5 mans unless you were trying to summon Anzu which required a druid to do it.

I raided as feral and tanked and DPSed plenty and was really liked for the utility I brought with my off heals, innervate, b-rez, and pick up the boss if the main tank died (So long as I was geared hybrid and not pure DPS). I wasn't topping lists most times then but I carried my own weight and saved many wipes. But when it came to 5 mans where you have to hope to have someone else pick up your missing baseline abilities, then its a massive uphill battle.

I rarely ever did Tree because it wasn't too fun for me, but I watched countless times where they were sidelined just due to their missing healing spell.

Now, in WotLK, they got the resurrection they should have had since vanilla and I went to consistently topping DPS charts but not as a hybrid anymore. Blizzard has a habit of refusing to fix many issues until they can break others. Just like they refused to let druids use potions and elixirs in forms until after they gutted most of the alchemy stuff first.

Giving druids a normal resurrection spell isn't the red line you fear it will be, it won't change its play style, it won't negatively impact anyone beyond maybe that priest, paladin or shaman who only got chosen over the druid because of that singular spell being the deciding factor which would be a good thing for server health overall.

I think most arguments have already been made, but I’m still trying different formats in the hope you’ll eventually understand — not accept, just *understand* my point.

 1. Yes, druids can heal — but they are a *hybrid* class designed to fill multiple roles. Having a healing spec doesn’t mean they must share the same baseline tools as every other healer.
 2. Druids *do* have a resurrection — in combat. That is part of their identity and a deliberate trade-off in their design.
 3. This *does* impact the game. Class identity matters. Giving every healer all the same tools is like letting paladins equip bows because “every class should have ranged.” It erodes uniqueness, which affects *everyone*.
 4. Adding both types of resurrection wouldn’t change moment-to-moment gameplay, but it *would* remove something iconic from the druid kit — and that’s a step toward homogenization.
 5. The “negative impact” you’re pointing to is about quality of life, not the quality of the game itself.

> **Fugus wrote:**
> You might not have played retail when this was a thing but I did...

Actually, I’ve played since the original release — through Maraudon, TBC, Wrath, Cataclysm, Pandaria, Legion — so I know exactly what happens when convenience-driven changes pile up. I was there when groups had to run back because the druid couldn’t revive. Yes, it was frustrating. But it also created social dynamics, friendships, and memorable moments tied to class identity.

These weren’t flaws to erase; they were part of the game’s social and mechanical fabric.

> **Fugus wrote:**
> When it came to 5 mans and heroics:
>  1. Cat and Moonkin wasn't wanted because...
>  2. Bear wasn't wanted because...
>  3. And the Tree wasn't wanted due to this singular issue...

I understand those frustrations, but Classic+ is not TBC retail. If Restoration druids being passed over is truly a problem, the fix would be to add a normal resurrection deep in the Restoration tree — not baseline to every spec. That way the solution addresses the concern *where it’s relevant* without erasing the original trade-offs.

> **Fugus wrote:**
> Now, in WotLK, they got the resurrection they should have had since vanilla...

WotLK also brought sweeping homogenization — and not all of it was healthy for the game. Druids here are already strong across DPS, healing, mitigation, and utility. Adding a no-CD resurrection to every spec is not a harmless QoL tweak; it’s a class design change with long-term consequences.

 **Honestly, it feels like you want to play TBC or WotLK here — and that’s not going to happen.**

1. Cat and Moonkin wasn't wanted because...
2. Bear wasn't wanted because...
3. And the Tree wasn't wanted due to this singular issue...
I understand those frustrations, but Classic+ is not TBC retail. If Restoration druids being passed over is truly a problem, the fix would be to add a normal resurrection deep in the Restoration tree — not baseline to every spec. That way the solution addresses the concern *where it’s relevant* without erasing the original trade-offs.
Now, in WotLK, they got the resurrection they should have had since vanilla...
WotLK also brought sweeping homogenization — and not all of it was healthy for the game. Druids here are already strong across DPS, healing, mitigation, and utility. Adding a no-CD resurrection to every spec is not a harmless QoL tweak; it’s a class design change with long-term consequences.

Honestly, it feels like you want to play TBC or WotLK here — and that’s not going to happen.

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Give Druids a Revive Spell
content_md:
Just thought I'd touch on this too actually because the hybrid argument makes zero sense:

All the other healing classes are hybrids.

Paladins can do every role. Shamans can do every role. Priests can also DPS. What do they all have?

The ability to heal or prevent damage

The ability to resurrect people

The ability to apply some sort of buff(s), whether it be blessings, prayers, totems or otherwise.

A bear druid, shadow priest, ele sham, ret paladin or other is, albeit sub-optimally, also a healer, because that's how being a HYBRID works. You can do multiple things. I've legit done runs of RFC where my role in the team comp wasn't concrete, because my kit barely let me tank, my spellcasting DPS was terrible, and my only form was bear. I did a bit of everything. This is, at its core, how druid functions thematically from 1-60 before specializing is important. Ferals throw on healing gear. DPS popping bear form to tank in a pinch. Other classes function the same. An enh sham can take threat to offtank. The shadow priest helps keep the team up with vampiric embrace or an offheal.

Now, imagine the frustration someone might have when being told that they, as a HEALING class, lack something as significant and group defining as a resurrect. Now imagine this situation.

You're the group healer. Your group consists of a mage, hunter, warrior, rogue, and you.

Someone does something stupid. Maybe a pet pulls a few too many mobs. Maybe someone had a connection issue. Maybe that big heal you needed on the tank didn't come out fast enough. For whatever reason, you- or more than one person... Has died.

No one can res.

You've failed to do your job as a healer. What did you do wrong?

Play druid.

Thank you for coming to my TED talk.

Most I've seen in class changes, is take away the established feeling of vanilla, giving all classes the base tools for the ESTABLISHED meta game "efficiency over everything" and "damage is all that matters". Essentially turning it into Retail, where we pick the S Tier class, over the class we actually like. Not that it matters in Retail anyway, since all classes play the exact same way but the visuals changed.

I get that we humans always want to work with the best tools. But TWoW has done nothing to make certain tools more useful in different situations, its become homogenized and generalized. You could argue they SHOULD give Paladins to Horde, because its cross factions raids now anyway, essentially completely unbalancing the factions bc Paladins were supposed to be the Shaman Counterpart for the Alliance. And then people like you come into a private server because you either HATE Blizzard, or dont like what they did to WoW as it stands now. And then proceed to turn it into Retail again, absolute Jokes.

TWoW shouldve played INTO the nicheness of the classes, essentially doubling down on it a LITTLE. Not too much.

 -----------------
Here id like to make some examples of how something should work in an RPG, or generally speaking, LOGICALLY.

A Mage - Pure DPS Class in Talents - should be able to be useful in a lot of raids (elemental weaknesses) due to
 1. Their Class Fantasy involving different kinds of elemental damage + being almost focused completely on destruction magic.
 2. Fulfulling their role in a group setting
 3. But they still shouldnt get a version of "blizzard" for every single element(I.e. Arcane Blizzard or smth), like shamans got additional casting DPS spells for a different school of magic in TWoW. If the situation simply doesnt ALLOW lightning to be effective, maybe bring another class as DPS for that specific dungeon or raid, shamans can HEAL. You shouldnt play a SPEC, you should play a CLASS.

A Shaman - Heal/DPS/Tank Hybrid - Should NOT excel in each of these categories, nor be completely useless (They BUFF The raid, that is their usefulness)
 1. In the Vanilla Setting it makes them one hit wonders, being able to DPS/HEAL/Tank their way out of everything. Good example of this would be a Warrior+Shaman group for questing. They can almost pull 7 mobs without dying, its that strong.
 2. In addition, TWoW gave shamans even MORE tools and spells just to amplify their damage. Amplyfing damage via extra Spells compared to the original, needs complete rebalancing of raids, mobs, dungeons. Just for the sake of adding ONE spell to ONE class, that only does DAMAGE.
 3. Turned complete Spec Talent Trees into better DPS than others. A Class with 3 DPS Specs, should be better at pure damage dealing, than a 2 spec or 1 spec class. Tanking is a different issue, you can't look at it the same way.

Paladins turn out to be more useful than Warriors because they now have the tools to Tank in ADDITION to their already baseline kit of incredible heal and buffing. As a Warrior Player myself, I can't think of myself being picked over a Paladin Tank.

Some vanilla specs may be shit, some to the point of Balance Druid, which deserve to get changes. And some to the point of Ret Paladin, which can excel at PvP and being an additional buffer support in raids, but sucked way more in damage compared to a MAGE or WARRIOR (3 and 2 DPS classes respectively). Ret got buffed to compete in DAMAGE once again, the only thing simple minded players see is their DPS. This is exactly why retail sucks now, and why people go to private servers.

Theres already a BUNCH of players that left TWoW behind because they noticed these changes. They are silent, they are gone, they dont voice their opinion. So you obviously will be in the "majority" of your opinions all the time. The vocal minority will always see themselves as the majority.

The players that left dis so because they knew it would deteriorate like this even further. Whether this is a good way to do it, is another point altogether.
Then there's the forum dwellers, who have apparently nothing better to do than discuss moot topics like this because they want to impose their on perspectual world view on the game, failing to understand the actual game design behind it. Then forcing me, a guy that normally doesnt go out of his way to make fools like you understand how WRONG you are, go on a coherent tangent like this.

I KNOW the point im making will get understood by maybe only 5% of you. And even if I can only make 1 of you realize that what most here are saying is complete BS, I've done my job well.

Priest should get BRez removed (didnt even know they had it). Druids have a POINT to existing. The BRez is a clutch spell and useful tool to even "cheese" some encounters.

author: Halfgeek9
subject: Balance Druids are getting nerfed in 1.8
content_md:
Are they doing too much dps? Nope. Mediocre currently.

In 1.8, two Balance Druid mechanics are nerfed:

Balance in All Thing Starfire cast time reduction nerfed from 0.8s to 0.5s. A big nerf to Starfire cast time. Instead of 2.2s its 2.5s. Or 2s with the Starfire idol, to 2.3s.

Eclipse nerfed from flat 30% damage bonus to 10% + 60% of spell crit rate.

T1 geared Balance Druids have around 20% spell crit. T2 geared around 25% spell crit. T3 geared around 30% spell crit.

 10% + (60% of 20%) = 22%

 10% + (60% of 25%) = 25%

To reach 30% Eclipse dmg bonus, a Balance Druid must have 34% spell crit.

Balance Druids do not have +spell crit talents like other casters, they only get +10% to Moonfire. Moonkin is grp 3% spell crit buff.

But what about Wrath/Starfire Eclipse proc buff?

Wrath has 30% chance to proc. That's about the crit rate of T3 Moonkins Wrath.

Starfire has 50% chance to proc Nature Eclipse, okay, that's a buff. But Arcane Eclipse is where Druid dps is good, because of Curse of Shadows in raids. Wrath being nature doesn't benefit, and get higher partial resists.

So we don't really get into Arcane Eclipse more often. And when we do, its less than the current 30% dmg bonus, and Starfires cast slower.

WTF why nerf Balance Druids?

author: Snkx
subject: Feral Feedback after raiding in 1.18
content_md:
The new changes have been mostly positive for Feral.

However the spec still has some flaws.

#1 - Bleed Immunes
While not as devastating as before, they are still a big DPS loss, also you still have to change your playstyle entirely (to Powershifting), yes Tiger's Fury now grants 10 energy per 3 seconds, but this is still around a 20% dps loss compared to powershifting, people who enjoy the non powershifting variant dont want to feel screwed over on bleed immune.

#2 - Powershifting itself.
Even on non bleed immunes, the Bleeds Regen + TF vastly outperform powershifting, so you will only use Powershifting as a "Plan B" as mentioned above. - I think the gap is still too big and needs closing more, Maybe a buff to Furor to grant 50 Energy instead of 40 could help.

#3 - Talent Point Issue.
We feel really starved for Talent points, heck ive got FOUR Feral specs just in my Brain Wash device, one for Tanking, one for PVP, one for DPS, and one for DPS outside (with feral swiftness and feral charge)

In raids I mostly DPS as Cat, so I have zero room for any bear talents, I cant take Charge, Feral Instinct (Threat Talent), Thick hide (minor) or Feral Swiftness (dodge), the devs freed up 2 talent points by merging Savage Fury and Predatory Strikes, which was great.... But then they added a new 2 pointer which took these points up anyway, so this didnt really help.

Personally I'd like to see atleast 3 talent points freed up so I can atleast pick up Feral charge and Swiftness in the DPS Cat Spec, after all when you look at Ep*chs talent tree you can take both Tank&DPS talents, which is how feral should be IMO.

#4 - The Tier sets / itemization.

Okay I think everyone can agree that the new Tier sets designed for Feral Cats, have a tad too much intellect on them, this really hurts our dps, and alot of people are rolling on the leather chest from Meph in Kara (Warrirors, Shamans, Rogues, Hunters), which we also want, even more so that we dont have a great tier option.
Personally I'd like to see some intellect removed, and restatted into either strength or agility, also cats dont gain much from +% attack speed, thats more a Bear stat for threat.

#5 - Consider just removing the restriction from form entirely.

You have now removed potions and jujus from the restricted in form list, which is great, but it just still feels inconsistant, if a Bear can crack the cork out of a potion and drink it, why cant he throw a grenade or sapper charge? it makes so sense, on another Server I can do all that and pick the flag up in Warsong and talk to NPCs etc, it just feels alot more fluid .... You've done 75% of the work, why restrict the rest of it from being used?

Anyway thats all I have for now. - I think the feral changes have been great, but I still feel like more could be done.

Ty

author: Familypanzer
subject: Druid Powershifting / Macros in general
content_md:
Hello everyone!

I have a couple of questions about the druid class on this server. Currently I have a level 24 druid. A bit of background; I played WoW back in vanilla and vanilla TBC though I don't remember much about the technical questions I have below. I again, played during classic, tbc classic, and wrath classic. I also played until lvl 40 of SoD until it just felt like all that was change was classes without an extension to the story. During my classic and SoD run I played druid. Love the class fantasy, mechanics, and utility. I actually like powershifting haha. I've recently had the itch to play classic when I randomly stumbled upon a Turtle Wow youtube video. My mind was blown, this is what I had been looking for! This was the missing link between classic and SoD. Needless to say, I'm happy to have found this server.

Playing druid in modern classic wow, I've been spoiled with druid macros. I understand the 1.12 client has limitations though addons have largely fixed those for me. author: Mcnair
subject: Re: Balance Druid – Can I Heal Dungeons While Leveling?
content_md:
Good day.
As long as you have an Intellect-heavy gear for healing (which you'll have if you plan on being Balance), you can surely heal all the instances as you level, unless your tank is underleveled or badly undergeared (e.g. fury warrior without a shield and in mostly leather DPS gear).
This in general true for all healer/hybrid classes, be it paladins, druids, shaman, or priest, they all can heal the instances as they come in any spec (or even without any talents) as long as they have an Intellect-heavy healing gear.
Just make sure to either have a mage or buy drinks before the start, as without a constant supply of drinks the downtimes will be rather insufferable. Also, do not try to be a miser with the said drinks, drink whenever you get out of combat and you have missing mana, as sadly many tanks tend to chainpull in instances disregarding healer mana.
This starts to change around level 50 or so, when the instances with higher mob density and overall higher damage start.

subject: Re: resto druid help
content_md:
Max rank for when you need to top someone up fast. Rest is downranked regrowths.

Which one? Depends on your gear, but as a rule of thumb, spam regrowth with full mana and no buffs/consumables. If your mana last 45 seconds or more without any external help/no innervate/ no potions you're good for 90% of the fights with that rank. If your mana lasts more than 1 min 15 secs use a higher rank and repeat until you're between 45 secs and 1 min 15 secs

content_md:
I main a resto druid, in a guild that is raiding on Ambershire.

In group content, a resto druid is ok, but we cannot compensate for an undergeared tank, where other healers sometimes can. This is because we have less up-front healing options, and our mana sustain can be tricky.

author: Bayanni
subject: Re: Druid healer question - new to twow
content_md:
There's a few different restored healer routes. Moonglow HT is still a thing and Aessina's Bloom really makes the throughput feel great, especially if a tree is already HoTing your target. I regularly get high or on top of the meters in raids up to naxx because of it.

Tree is good but limited due to not having a solid repeatable heal for tanks. They're solid for a raid but I'd hold off using them as dungeon healers unless you're stacked and your HoTs alone can keep the MT up. The issue of multiple trees was alleviated somewhat with early HoT renewals granting some instant healing but it's not sustainable manager wise.

I still recommend tree over moonglow early in raiding since there's not a lot of competition for non-set healing pieces with high spirit (1spirit is 0.2 healing to every member of your party, so in a way every point of spirit is 1sp, very strong even if your personal logs don't reflect it) but be open to switching if there's already a lot of trees or there is a strong need in your team for direct heals on the tanks.

There is a third spec but I'm still evaluating but looks promising, going deep restored without tree or moonglow. If it holds up I'll post here unless someone can give their own evaluation first.

author: Frantsel
subject: Re: Resto Druids in BGs - Possible to survive Rogue stunlock?
content_md:
If its a good rogue: u are dead. If its a bad rogue with envenom, you might be also dead.

Best way is to be VERY fast with pvp trinket right after the first cheapshot or if he opens with ambush then after the kidney hits. Then run with travelform. 4 piece is kinda crucial to survive. I would always use 4 piece pvp set even if you have better gear. The speed bonus will save your life MANY times.

If the rogue tries to follow with sprint, nature's grasp, root. Whatever you think is safer to use. It depends how far you are away. Feral charge into stun can be an option to run away and restealth.

Focus on stamina gear over anything else. Be in bearform or stealth if you expect to be attacked. Use orb of deception to make it harder for the enemy to see your actual form. This helps especially in groupbattles.

You can fight some rogues in bearform if you have hp advantage. Be careful with that bearheal, it eats all you rage.
Use feral barkskin. Stun.

Rogues MELT druids. Even in bearform if they are assa spec.

But to be honest: Turtle pvp is utter garbage. Im glad that I stopped playing. This server just sucks for pvp.

Lately I’ve noticed something in BGs that’s been bugging me. In clutch moments, once I’ve already applied Rejuvenation and Regrowth, used Nature’s Swiftness + Healing Touch, and Swiftmend is on cooldown, I’m left with basically one option: spam Regrowth.

The problem is, Regrowth spam absolutely drains mana, and Healing Touch is way too slow to rely on in active PvP fights. Is there really no way around this? Are resto druids just designed to rely on other healers for those fast 1.5-second burst heals like priests, paladins, and shamans all have?

On my priest, for example, I rarely even touch Greater Heal because it’s too slow, but at least I’ve got Flash Heal to keep people alive in emergencies. It feels like druids just don’t have that equivalent until WotLK, when we finally get Nourish as a proper 1.5-second direct heal.

Curious how other druids handle this. Do you just pre-HoT and pray, or is there some trick I’m missing?

author: Scattyau
subject: The Current State of Boomkin
content_md:
I posted this to Reddit and was told I should crosspost it here. Yes, there are some issues with my haste comments and I added an edit, but didn't change the original content, so grain of salt that part. TLDR, Haste isn't as bad as I say, but Crit is still better. Also, I don't hate Fire Shaman, it is just a very apt comparison. My points would be the same in a vacuum if Fire Shaman was not how it is right now.

 -------------------------------------------------------------

Hey all. Scattyshifts here - 9/9 K40 and newly Scythe-touting Balance Druid Main here. Today, I'm here to tell you why Boomkin isn't rewarding to play. Its cool. Its viable. When you factor in raid comp, its great. But it doesn't feel rewarding.

The Competition
It would not be right to write this without context. So, I will be writing this knowing that Fire Shaman exists in its current state. For anyone unfamiliar, Fire Shaman has two buttons - Flame Shock, which fully snapshots trinkets etc, and Molten Blast, a 2s cast with excellent damage, double proccing from Rekindled Flame, and it refreshes your DOT duration on every single cast. You shock, then you Molten Blast for the whole fight, and you win DPS on Patchwerk. It is not engaging, but given its absurd simplicity and resistance to RNG, skill issues, or anything else, it massively overperforms and will almost definitely get a nerf. Arcane Mages, various flavours of Warlocks, even nature-based elemental Shamans all are in great places, and they play in ways that are rewarding and fun, but I need to call out Fire Shaman specifically because it overperforms with NO RNG and NO SKILL required. Which brings us to...

Performance
A full-BIS Boomkin, playing a perfect rotation with perfect 100%-chance Eclipse procs and lining up the next spells perfectly to benefit from Eclipses, standing still against a target dummy, will do LESS DPS than an equally geared Fire Shaman who used trinkets for their shock and have leaned on their Molten Blast button. To be clear, a Druid with 100% proc chance on their RNG rotation-defining talent, perfect play, practically impossible to achieve, will do less damage than the '1' spammer Shaman. This is important context as well - people will overlook a LOT of issues if meters/parses say #1. Unfortunately, we're not top, so we need to actually have a rewarding playstyle to make up for it. Lame, right? But the problem with that is...

RNG Punishes
For many classes, RNG will give you a proc that you can take advantage of. A new button lights up, and when you press it, bigger numbers happen. Warlocks get Nightfall - if they need to move, they can instantly throw their nuke for some free bonus damage while repositioning, or just use it anyway since its still a good bonus. Neato!

The Boomkin rotation is full of RNG, and all of it is punishing.

Firstly, Eclipse. Eclipse procs 50% of the time on a Starfire, or 30% of the time from Wrath *hits*. Given that, as casters, we are chain casting, if you are in your "fishing for Eclipse" phase, you're chain casting one spell. So, when you get the notification that your Eclipse has actually procced, you're already casting your next spell. This can often mean that if you are hard-casting a 3s Starfire, and your last cast procced your Nature Eclipse, it is better to CANCEL the cast, write off the whole 1.5s GCD, and instead begin chain casting Wrath. It feels SO BAD to literally cancel a cast because it isn't worth finishing it, and you have a buff ticking down that you need to make the most of. On the flip side, your Arcane Eclipse procs off the Wrath HITTING the target, and it has a hell of a travel time. So you will almost always lose at least 1, often 2-3, seconds of your 15 second buff because you were GCD locked into your "fishing" spell when the payoff landed.

Next, DOTs. Eclipse's damage buff is so high, it is mathematically worth clipping your DOTs at a certain point to refresh them with the Eclipse bonus. However, we have two DOTs with practically identical durations, and given the chaincasting nature of Boomkin, you really want to refresh them together. Optimal play means refreshing one with Eclipse out of sync, and so it feels gross to play. You're often clipping DOTs, or going without one briefly, because your casts and your lunar cycle don't play nice with DOT durations.

Next, Balance of All Things. There is so much to hate here. Firstly, they recharge randomly and unpredictably, with a 30% on each DOT tick. Second, the Starfire buff is great, reducing the cast time, but with 3 charges stacked, it is gone in 6 seconds of back-to-back crits and now you're back to hard casting 3s spells. The Wrath bonus is... well, a mana discount is welcome, but it objectively doesn't affect how you play. Neither of these really affect your decision making, the Starfire one feels good for the three charges but the odds you will recharge one before your Eclipse ends there are around a coin flip, so you're definitely spending the rest of the Eclipse and subsequent fishing phase on 3s casts, sans crits. But also, it can just NOT proc, and then it feels TERRIBLE to enter Arcane Eclipse with a 3s hard cast. It is absolutely possible to get only FOUR Starfires off in a whole Eclipse, less if you need to re-DOT. Also, our 5p T3.5 bonus, the best set in game right now, increases this lacklustre effect by 50%, so you can feel so little, slightly more! Drop your Wrath down to 37 mana, 3 times!

Also, Haste. Druid Atiesh gives Haste, our set is loaded with Haste, and our T3 8-piece bonus is Haste. Haste affects ONE of our FOUR spells. Wrath is GCD capped with 0 haste, and the two DOTs don't scale with it. So, Starfire gets Haste. Feels Bad Man, especially when Crit triple-dips by increasing damage per cast, proccing Nature's Grace for far better haste, and also increasing the Eclipse multiplier. My calculations put 1% crit equal to around 4-5% Haste. It might even be worse. But it is hard to avoid it.

 *EDIT: Moriena pointed out, Haste's GCD is 1.0s base, 0.5s with talent. So it still benefits from Haste. So this point is less pronounced, but Haste is still significantly worse than Crit but it is thrust at us from multiple places. Happy to be wrong, but it doesn't make it all better.*

Oh, and our Best Idol? Two choices. One, the best by my calculations, is a BOE that gives 17% Moonfire damage that scales with Spellpower. Just insane. Moonfire is around 22% of our damage, so increasing it by 17% is close to a 4% total DPS gain from the Idol slot. The other, Ebb And Flow, reduces Starfire cast time. The one spell that gets Haste, gets a bit more. It isn't bad, but given Starfire is our 4th best spell and we'd rather cast anything else, it is nowhere near as good as it FEELS. It FEELS great casting faster Starfires, but the actual damage impact is less than Mr 17% Moonfire over there, who sells for a lick under 20g right now and is BIS forever.

Overall, every single RNG talent feels like you have a ticking clock that is wasting away while you're locked into casting something else, or they're inconsequential until you just happened to NOT get them, then it just feels bad. There is no "oh yay, I got X, I can do this now", it is only "Fuck, of course it procced now..." or "where the hell is my X?"

Talent Bloat
This would not be complete without discussing talents. Firstly, Genesis in Resto is too strong to pass up, so you have 13 points in Resto. Thankfully this is improved from last patch, where we needed 18. However, we're still bloated with 38 points in Balance.

Firstly, you need the Core Talents. Everthing that increases damage, hit, range, crit, cast times, Moonkin Form, BoAT, Eclipse. That is 35 points. So, we have 3 points to flex, between interruption avoidance, improved moonkin form, gale winds, or any utility cross-tree. Improved Moonkin Form is a one-point wonder, since the only scaling is the cooldown going 30/25/20 seconds. So, two points, either gale winds or avoiding interruption. Gale Winds is amazing raid utility, but it adds no damage, so most go with interrupt avoidance, but it still brings you to 76% during an enraged owlkin proc, so you still get pushback.

Solutions
 *"Players are normally almost always right about problems, that's the thing I always find. They're almost never right about the solutions."* - Sean Murray, No Man's Sky creator.

With that in mind, the goal should be making it so when an RNG proc happens, you can take advantage of it without feeling that it is being wasted, and it should feel impactful.

First, Talents. Remove Moonfury - it is flat damage early in the tree on a tier with 10 other points. That frees up 3 points to get either all the Balance Tools, OR to hybrid into Resto further. Roll the damage bonus into Moonkin Form, or just increase the baseline spell damage. Moonkin Form gives the aura and armour, with a small mana discount, it is much less impactful than every other form that gives new abilities etc, or Tree with its massive healing bonus.

Balance of All Things should be something you want to see saved up, and spend the charges. This would actually much more be suited to the flat damage bonus Eclipse currently gives - save up bonus damage charges, and use them on demand when the lunar cycle is right, giving you more control over your playstyle and conscious payoff.
